This is a lighter-weight alternative to the parallel fund described in Option 3.

**3. Recommendation. Feeder funds are not recommended at this time for initial fund formation.** The identified anchor investors are individually of sufficient size to invest directly in the main Fund, and the fundraising strategy does not currently contemplate the aggregation of smaller commitments through a feeder vehicle. If sagebrush\'s marketing efforts identify a group of smaller institutional investors or family offices that would benefit from feeder fund aggregation, this option can be revisited during the fundraising process.

If a feeder fund is ultimately adopted, it would be formed as a Delaware limited partnership (for U.S. investors) or an offshore entity (for non-U.S. investors) and would subscribe as a single limited partner in the main Fund. The feeder fund\'s terms would replicate the main Fund\'s economic terms, and its governing document would address the allocation of governance rights and reporting obligations to the feeder fund\'s underlying investors.

**[V. RECOMMENDED ENTITY HIERARCHY AND ORGANIZATIONAL CHART]{.underline}**

Based on our analysis in Section IV, we recommend the following entity hierarchy for CLSO Fund I. The entities described below fall into three categories: (A) core entities to be formed as part of the initial fund formation process; (B) existing entities that play a role in the fund structure; and (C) contingent entities to be formed only if and when specific conditions are met.

**[A. Core Entities (To Be Formed)]{.underline}**

**1. Cobalt Life Sciences Opportunities Fund I, LP**

**Entity type:** Delaware limited partnership, formed under the DRULPA.

**Role:** The Fund --- the primary investment vehicle for the Fund\'s investment program. All portfolio investments will be made by or through the Fund (directly or through AIVs, the blocker corporation, or the parallel fund, as applicable).

**General Partner:** Cobalt Life Sciences GP I, LLC.

**Limited Partners:** Institutional investors (including Ironwood PERS, Northgate, Pinnacle, and additional investors sourced by sagebrush), as well as the General Partner in its capacity as a limited partner for the GP commitment.

**Governing Document:** Limited Partnership Agreement (the \"LPA\"), to be entered into by the General Partner and all limited partners. Target first draft circulation: May 31, 2026.

**2. Cobalt Life Sciences GP I, LLC**

**Entity type:** Delaware limited liability company, formed under the Delaware Limited Liability Company Act, 6 Del. C. §§18-101 *et seq.*

**Role:** The General Partner of the Fund. Responsible for all fund management and investment decisions, subject to the terms of the LPA. Holds the carried interest entitlement.

**Managing Members:** Dr. Marcus Yeung and Priya Dasgupta.

**Carried Interest Allocation:** The carried interest entitlement is allocated among the principals as follows: Dr. Marcus Yeung --- 55%; Priya Dasgupta --- 35%; Alan Whitford --- 10%. The specific mechanics of this allocation will be set forth in the GP LLC Agreement and any ancillary carried interest allocation agreements.

**GP Commitment:** The General Partner will make the GP commitment on behalf of the principals --- a minimum of two percent (2%) of aggregate commitments, equaling \$15,000,000 at the target fund size of \$750 million. The GP commitment will be invested on the same terms as LP commitments (drawn pro rata, returned pro rata) and will not be subject to the management fee.

**Governing Document:** LLC Operating Agreement (the \"GP LLC Agreement\"), to be entered into by Dr. Yeung, Ms. Dasgupta, and Mr. Whitford. Target first draft: May 31, 2026.

**3. Cobalt Life Sciences Management I, LLC**

**Entity type:** Delaware limited liability company.

**Role:** The Management Company. Employs the Fund\'s investment professionals (Dr. Yeung, Ms. Dasgupta, Mr. Whitford, and future hires). Receives the management fee from the Fund. Bears organizational expenses in excess of the \$1,500,000 cap. Implements management fee offset mechanics (100% offset for placement fees paid to sagebrush; 80% offset for transaction and monitoring fees received from portfolio companies).

**Registration:** If full registration under the Advisers Act is required (as analyzed by Fielding & O\'Hara), the Management Company (or Cobalt Ventures LP, depending on entity-level registration analysis) would serve as the registered investment adviser.

**Governing Document:** LLC Operating Agreement (the \"Management Company LLC Agreement\"). Target first draft: May 31, 2026.

**4. Cobalt Life Sciences Opportunities Fund I (Blocker), Inc.**

**Entity type:** Delaware C-corporation, formed under the Delaware General Corporation Law, 8 Del. C. §§101 *et seq.* To be formed **if and when needed** based on confirmed investor participation requiring blocker access.

**Role:** The blocker Corporation. Interposes between tax-sensitive investors (Pinnacle, and potentially Northgate) and the Fund or specific portfolio investments. Absorbs income at the corporate level and distributes after-tax earnings to its shareholders as dividends, thereby blocking the flow-through of UBTI, ECI, or insurance-unfavorable income to its investors.

**Formation Trigger:** Confirmed participation by Pinnacle Insurance Group or Northgate Endowment Management (or other investors) requiring blocker access.

**Governing Document:** Certificate of Incorporation and Bylaws. To be drafted in connection with blocker formation.

**[B. Existing Entity (Sponsor)]{.underline}**

**Cobalt Ventures LP**

**Entity type:** Delaware limited partnership (DE LP File No. 7824931; CA SOS File No. 202118412387; EIN: 83-2947561).

**Role:** The Sponsor. Cobalt Ventures LP serves as the ultimate sponsor and brand entity for the Fund, but does not play a direct structural role in the Fund\'s entity hierarchy. Cobalt Ventures LP will not serve as the general partner, management company, or a limited partner of the Fund.

Cobalt Ventures LP may provide certain shared services to CLSO Management I, LLC --- such as office space, back-office support, information technology infrastructure, and other operational resources --- under an inter-company services arrangement. This arrangement should be documented in a written services agreement (a separate workstream) to ensure arm\'s-length terms and appropriate allocation of costs, and to comply with any regulatory requirements applicable to the Management Company as a registered (or exempt reporting) investment adviser.

**[C. Contingent Entities]{.underline}**

**Parallel Fund (Name TBD)**

A parallel fund vehicle, to be organized as a Delaware limited partnership, an offshore limited partnership, or another appropriate entity form. **To be formed only if non-U.S. investor demand reaches or exceeds \$50 million.** The parallel fund would invest alongside the main Fund on a pro rata basis, on identical economic and governance terms, with aggregated waterfall economics. The main Fund\'s LPA will include parallel fund enabling provisions that authorize the General Partner to form the parallel fund without LP consent.

**Alternative Investment Vehicles (AIVs)**

One or more special-purpose entities (typically Delaware LLCs or LPs, or offshore entities as appropriate), to be formed on a **deal-by-deal or investor-by-investor basis** as authorized under the LPA\'s AIV provisions. AIVs will be formed only when a specific tax, legal, regulatory, or operational need arises, and will invest alongside the main Fund on substantially the same economic terms.

**Feeder Fund(s).** Standalone feeder vehicles (domestic or offshore), **not currently planned** and reserved as a future option. May be formed if fundraising dynamics warrant the aggregation of smaller investor commitments or the creation of a dedicated vehicle for a specific investor category. If formed, the feeder fund would subscribe as a single limited partner in the main Fund.

**[D. Organizational Chart]{.underline}**

The following describes the organizational structure of CLSO Fund I and its related entities. A preliminary organizational chart diagram will be provided as **Attachment A** to this memorandum.

**Sponsor Level:**

> Cobalt Ventures LP (Sponsor) --- existing entity; serves as the brand and operational platform for the Cobalt fund family.

**Management Level:**

> Cobalt Life Sciences Management I, LLC (Management Company) --- receives management fee from the Fund; employs investment professionals; connected to Cobalt Ventures LP via inter-company services arrangement.

**General Partner Level:**

> Cobalt Life Sciences GP I, LLC (General Partner) --- managed by Dr. Yeung and Ms. Dasgupta; holds carried interest entitlement; makes GP commitment; serves as general partner of the Fund.

**Fund Level:**

> Cobalt Life Sciences Opportunities Fund I, LP (the Fund) --- primary investment vehicle; the General Partner sits above as general partner; limited partners invest directly. The blocker Corporation (Cobalt Life Sciences Opportunities Fund I (Blocker), Inc.) is shown with a dotted line connection to the Fund, indicating its contingent status --- the blocker is interposed between certain limited partners (Pinnacle, potentially Northgate) and the Fund. AIV entities are shown with dotted lines alongside the Fund, indicating their contingent, deal-specific formation. The Parallel Fund is shown with a dotted line alongside the Fund, indicating its contingent formation if non-U.S. investor demand warrants.

**Portfolio Level:**

> Portfolio Companies --- the Fund (together with AIVs, the blocker Corporation, and the Parallel Fund, as applicable) invests in clinical-stage therapeutics companies, medical device companies, and platform biotechnology companies.

**[VI. GENERAL PARTNER AND MANAGEMENT COMPANY --- STRUCTURAL CONSIDERATIONS]{.underline}**

**[A. Separation of GP and Management Company]{.underline}**

We recommend that the General Partner entity (CLSO GP I, LLC) and the Management Company entity (CLSO Management I, LLC) be organized as **separate legal entities**, each formed as a Delaware limited liability company. The separation of the GP and Management Company functions into distinct entities is market-standard for institutional-grade fund structures and serves several important purposes:

**Liability Isolation.** The General Partner bears unlimited liability for the obligations of the Fund as a matter of Delaware partnership law. By separating the General Partner from the Management Company, the employment-related and operational liabilities of the Management Company (including employee claims, lease obligations, vendor contracts, and regulatory obligations) are contained within the Management Company and do not directly expose the General Partner to additional liability beyond its partnership obligations. Conversely, the General Partner\'s partnership liabilities (including its obligations under the clawback provision and its joint and several liability among the principals) are contained within the GP entity and do not directly expose the Management Company\'s assets.

**Economic Clarity.** The economic flows to the two entities are distinct: carried interest flows through the General Partner, while management fee revenue flows to the Management Company. This separation provides clear economic attribution for tax, accounting, and regulatory purposes, and simplifies the analysis of conflicts of interest and fee-offset calculations.

**Market Standard.** The vast majority of institutional-quality private investment funds with which we are familiar --- including virtually all funds at or above the \$500 million target size --- employ separate GP and Management Company entities. Institutional limited partners and their investment consultants expect and are comfortable with this structure.

Both entities will be formed as Delaware LLCs. The LLC operating agreements for the GP (the \"GP LLC Agreement\") and the Management Company (the \"Management Company LLC Agreement\") will be prepared as separate workstreams, with target first drafts to be circulated to the principals on May 31, 2026, concurrent with the first draft of the LPA.

**[B. GP Commitment Mechanics]{.underline}**

The General Partner will make a commitment to the Fund as a limited partner, equal to a minimum of **two percent (2%) of aggregate commitments**. At the target fund size of \$750 million, this equates to a GP commitment of **\$15,000,000**. This commitment level is consistent with market expectations for first-time funds and demonstrates meaningful alignment of interest between the Sponsor\'s principals and the Fund\'s limited partners.

The source of the GP commitment will be personal capital from the Fund\'s principals --- Dr. Yeung, Ms. Dasgupta, and Mr. Whitford --- and/or capital from Cobalt Ventures LP. The proportions in which the GP commitment is funded by each principal (and by Cobalt Ventures LP, if applicable) will be determined by the principals in consultation with their personal tax and financial advisors, and will be documented in the GP LLC Agreement and the Fund\'s subscription documents.

The GP commitment will be invested on the **same terms as LP commitments**: drawn pro rata with LP capital calls, returned pro rata with distributions, and subject to the same distribution waterfall (including the preferred return and carried interest mechanics). The GP commitment will **not be subject to the management fee**, which is consistent with market practice (the management fee compensates the Management Company for services provided to the Fund, and charging a management fee on the GP\'s own capital would be economically circular).

The GP commitment will be reflected in the Fund\'s capital accounts and will participate in gains and losses on the same basis as LP capital. For purposes of calculating the 25% plan asset threshold under ERISA (discussed in Section VII.A), the GP commitment is generally excluded from the denominator, as the GP\'s interest is not a \"class of equity interests\" within the meaning of DOL Reg. §2510.3-101.

**[C. Key Person Provisions]{.underline}**

The LPA will designate **Dr. Marcus Yeung** and **Priya Dasgupta** as the Fund\'s \"Key Persons.\" The Key Person provision is a critical governance mechanism that protects limited partners\' investment by ensuring that the principals whose expertise and judgment are central to the Fund\'s investment strategy remain actively engaged in the Fund\'s operations throughout the investment period.

**Trigger.** The Key Person event will be triggered if either Key Person ceases to devote **substantially all** of his or her business time to the affairs of the Fund. The \"substantially all\" standard is the market-standard formulation and is generally understood to mean that the Key Person\'s primary professional activity is the management of the Fund and the performance of the Management Company\'s obligations thereunder, with limited exceptions for personal investments, charitable activities, and industry board memberships that do not materially interfere with the Key Person\'s responsibilities to the Fund.

**Consequence.** Upon the occurrence of a Key Person event, the **investment period will be suspended** --- the General Partner will not be permitted to make new investments or draw down additional capital for new investments (although commitments for follow-on investments in existing portfolio companies and investments for which binding commitments have been made prior to the Key Person event will generally be permitted). The investment period suspension will continue until the limited partners vote, by a specified majority (to be determined in the LPA, typically a majority-in-interest of limited partners excluding the GP\'s interest), to either (a) **reinstate** the investment period (with or without the designation of a replacement Key Person) or (b) **terminate** the investment period.

**Structural Implication.** The GP LLC Agreement should contain provisions requiring each Key Person to devote substantially all of his or her business time to the affairs of the Fund and the Management Company, and restricting each Key Person\'s outside activities during the Fund\'s term. These provisions should be consistent with the Key Person obligations set forth in the LPA, and should provide for appropriate consequences (including potential forfeiture or reduction of carried interest) in the event of a Key Person\'s breach of the devotion-of-time obligation. The specific terms of the Key Person restrictions in the GP LLC Agreement will be coordinated with the LPA provisions and are part of the GP LLC Agreement drafting workstream.

**[VII. ERISA AND VCOC CONSIDERATIONS]{.underline}**

**[A. Plan Asset Analysis]{.underline}**

The Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974, as amended (\"ERISA\"), imposes fiduciary obligations on persons who manage the assets of employee benefit plans. Under regulations promulgated by the Department of Labor (\"DOL\"), specifically DOL Reg. §2510.3-101 (as modified by Section 3(42) of ERISA), if **\"benefit plan investors\"** hold twenty-five percent (25%) or more of any class of equity interests in the Fund (excluding interests held by the General Partner, the Management Company, and their affiliates), the Fund\'s underlying assets will be treated as **\"plan assets\"** for purposes of ERISA. If the Fund\'s assets are treated as plan assets, the General Partner and the Management Company will be subject to ERISA\'s fiduciary duties (including the duties of prudence and loyalty) and prohibited transaction rules, which impose significant operational constraints and potential personal liability on the Fund\'s managers.

\"Benefit plan investors\" is defined broadly to include employee benefit plans subject to ERISA, plans subject to Section 4975 of the Internal Revenue Code (including individual retirement accounts), and entities whose underlying assets include plan assets by reason of a plan\'s investment in such entity. The definition may also encompass certain governmental plans and church plans, depending on the specific regulatory analysis.

**Application to the Fund\'s Anticipated Investor Base.** The anticipated investor base includes:

> • **Ironwood PERS** --- a state government pension fund organized under Oregon law. Governmental plans are generally not subject to ERISA (they are excluded from ERISA\'s coverage under ERISA §4(b)(1)). However, governmental plan assets may be counted as \"benefit plan investor\" assets for purposes of the 25% threshold under certain interpretations of DOL Reg. §2510.3-101. The regulatory analysis is not entirely settled on this point, and conservative fund sponsors typically count governmental plan assets in the 25% calculation.
>
> • **Northgate Endowment Management** --- a university endowment. Whether Northgate constitutes a \"benefit plan investor\" depends on its specific legal structure. If the endowment is a commingled investment vehicle that includes assets of employee benefit plans (such as the university\'s defined benefit pension plan or defined contribution plan), it may be treated as a benefit plan investor to the extent that plan assets are invested in the endowment. Northgate\'s specific structure should be confirmed during the subscription process.

**Monitoring.** We recommend that the Fund monitor the 25% benefit plan investor threshold at each closing and on an ongoing basis. The subscription agreement and investor questionnaire should require each limited partner to disclose its status as a benefit plan investor (or the percentage of its assets that constitute plan assets) and to notify the Fund of any change in status. Halcyon Fund Services should be engaged to track the 25% threshold as part of its fund administration responsibilities.

**[B. VCOC Election]{.underline}**

To avoid plan asset treatment even if benefit plan investors hold 25% or more of the Fund\'s equity interests, the Fund will elect to qualify as a **\"venture capital operating company\" (VCOC)** under DOL Reg. §2510.3-101(d). The VCOC exception provides that the assets of a VCOC are not treated as plan assets for purposes of ERISA, regardless of the level of benefit plan investor participation.

**VCOC Requirements.** To qualify as a VCOC, the Fund must satisfy two requirements:

> \(i\) **Investment Test.** At least fifty percent (50%) of the Fund\'s assets (valued at cost, at the time of each investment and on the last day of each annual valuation period thereafter) must be invested in **\"venture capital investments.\"** A \"venture capital investment\" is defined as an investment in an operating company with respect to which the Fund obtains **\"management rights\"** --- contractual rights that give the Fund the right to substantially participate in or substantially influence the management of the operating company. Management rights may take the form of board seats, board observer rights, contractual consultation rights, veto rights over specified management decisions, or other governance provisions.
>
> \(ii\) **Exercise Test.** The Fund must **actually exercise** management rights with respect to at least one portfolio company during each annual valuation period. Passive governance rights are not sufficient --- the Fund must affirmatively participate in or influence the management of at least one portfolio company.

**Application to CLSO Fund I.** The Fund\'s investment strategy is well-suited for VCOC qualification. The Fund targets board seats or contractual governance rights in one hundred percent (100%) of its portfolio companies. The Fund\'s check sizes (\$30 million to \$100 million) and focus on clinical-stage therapeutics, medical devices, and platform biotechnology companies ensure that the Fund\'s portfolio companies are \"operating companies\" within the meaning of the regulation. Accordingly, we expect the Fund to satisfy the 50% investment test with substantial margin, and to readily satisfy the exercise test through active board participation and governance involvement with portfolio companies.

**LPA Provisions.** The LPA should include VCOC-related covenants, including:

> • An obligation of the General Partner to use commercially reasonable efforts to **maintain VCOC status** throughout the Fund\'s term.
>
> • A right (but not obligation) of the General Partner to **refuse subscriptions** from, or limit transfers by, investors whose participation would jeopardize the Fund\'s VCOC qualification (for example, by causing the Fund\'s benefit plan investor percentage to exceed a level at which VCOC qualification becomes critical).
>
> • An obligation of the General Partner to obtain management rights in connection with each investment and to exercise management rights as required to satisfy the VCOC exercise test.

**VCOC Testing.** Ongoing VCOC compliance testing --- including annual verification of the 50% investment test and documentation of the exercise of management rights --- will be coordinated with **Halcyon Fund Services, Inc.** (Thomas Varga, Director -- Private Equity Administration) as part of the Fund\'s ongoing fund administration. Halcyon will maintain records of the cost basis of each investment, the management rights obtained in connection with each investment, and evidence oftion summarizes the key service providers and the scope of their engagement. Formal engagement agreements with each service provider will be executed as part of the fund formation process on the timelines set forth in Section XII.

**[A. Fund Administrator]{.underline}**

**Halcyon Fund Services, Inc.** Thomas Varga, Director -- Private Equity Administration 1735 Market Street, Suite 2200, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania 19103

Halcyon Fund Services has been selected to serve as the Fund\'s third-party administrator. Halcyon is an established private fund administration firm with significant experience administering life-sciences and healthcare-focused private investment funds. The scope of Halcyon\'s engagement will include:

> • Net asset value (\"NAV\") calculations (quarterly, or more frequently as required by investor agreements)
>
> • Capital call and distribution processing, including preparation and distribution of capital call notices and distribution notices to limited partners
>
> • Investor reporting, including quarterly and annual investor statements, capital account balances, and IRR/TVPI performance metrics
>
> • AML/KYC screening of investors in connection with subscriptions
>

>

>
> • Coordination with the independent auditor on annual financial statement preparation

**[B. Independent Auditor]{.underline}**

**Whitfield & Pratt LLP** Maria Sandoval, Partner -- Private Funds Assurance 155 North Wacker Drive, Suite 4400, Chicago, Illinois 60606

Whitfield & Pratt LLP has been selected to serve as the Fund\'s independent auditor. Whitfield & Pratt is registered with the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (\"PCAOB\") and has a dedicated private funds assurance practice with experience auditing life-sciences and healthcare-focused private investment funds. The scope of Whitfield & Pratt\'s engagement will include:

>

**[C. Tax Advisor]{.underline}**

**Greystone Tax Advisors LLC** Kenneth Liu, Managing Director 44 Montgomery Street, Suite 3100, San Francisco, California 94104

Greystone Tax Advisors has been engaged to provide tax advisory services to the Fund. Greystone is a specialized tax advisory firm with deep experience in the taxation of private investment funds and their investors. The scope of Greystone\'s engagement includes:

> • Tax structuring advice, including UBTI/ECI planning, blocker entity analysis, and state income tax nexus analysis
>

>

Greystone\'s work is coordinated with Leonard Cross (Specialist Partner, Tax) at Calderwood & Harkness LLP, who is responsible for the Tax Structuring Memorandum delivered concurrently with this memorandum.

**[D. Insurance]{.underline}**

**Vantage Risk Advisors, Inc.** Laura Benton 30 Hudson Yards, Suite 6100, New York, New York 10001

Vantage Risk Advisors has been engaged as the Fund\'s insurance broker. Vantage will place **directors\' and officers\' liability insurance (\"D&O\")** and **errors and omissions insurance (\"E&O\")** on behalf of the Fund, the General Partner, the Management Company, and the individual principals and officers. The scope of coverage will include:

> • D&O coverage for the General Partner\'s managing members (Dr. Yeung and Ms. Dasgupta) and the Management Company\'s officers and employees
>
> • E&O coverage for professional liability arising from the Management Company\'s investment management and advisory activities
>
> • Coverage for the Fund\'s directors serving on portfolio company boards, to the extent not covered by portfolio company D&O policies

Insurance premiums are classified as **fund-level operating expenses** borne by the Fund under the LPA, consistent with market practice.

The insurance placement process is targeted for completion in **October 2026**, prior to the first close.

**[E. Placement Agent]{.underline}**

**sagebrush Capital Partners LLC** Jonathan Mercer, Managing Director 200 Park Avenue, 30th Floor, New York, New York 10166

Sagebrush Capital Partners has been engaged as the Fund\'s **exclusive global placement agent**. Sagebrush is a registered broker-dealer (SEC-registered; CRD No. 298714; FINRA member) specializing in private fund placements, with a focus on healthcare and life-sciences investment funds. Sagebrush\'s counsel is **Ashworth & Lyle LLP** (Sara Phan, Partner -- Investment Funds; 1251 Avenue of the Americas, 40th Floor, New York, New York 10020).

The key terms of sagebrush\'s engagement are as follows:

> • **Exclusivity:** sagebrush serves as the exclusive global placement agent for the Fund. All third-party investor introductions and placement activities are conducted by or through sagebrush, with the exception of investors introduced directly by the Cobalt principals (whose commitments are not subject to placement fees).
>
> • **Fee:** 1.50% of third-party commitments sourced by sagebrush, payable upon the closing at which the relevant investor is admitted to the Fund.
>

>
> • **Tail Period:** 24 months following termination of the placement agent agreement. Sagebrush is entitled to receive placement fees on commitments from investors introduced by sagebrush during the term of the engagement, even if such commitments are made during the tail period.
>
> • **Fee Offset:** 100% of placement fees paid to sagebrush are offset against the management fee payable by the Fund to the Management Company, over the life of the Fund.
>
> • **Governing Law:** New York.

The placement agent agreement is a separate document targeted for execution on **July 15, 2026**. Calderwood & Harkness will review and negotiate the agreement in coordination with Ashworth & Lyle.

**[F. Regulatory Counsel]{.underline}**

**Fielding & O\'Hara PLLC** Brian Liddell, Partner -- Investment Management 1625 Eye Street NW, Suite 900, Washington, DC 20006

Fielding & O\'Hara PLLC has been engaged to advise Cobalt on regulatory compliance matters, with a focus on Advisers Act compliance, Form ADV preparation and filing, and related regulatory filings. Fielding & O\'Hara\'s work is coordinated with Calderwood & Harkness\'s fund structuring and formation work. Brian Liddell is a recognized authority on investment management regulation and has extensive experience advising emerging and established fund managers on regulatory compliance.

**[XI. GOVERNANCE STRUCTURE --- LP ADVISORY COMMITTEE]{.underline}**

The LPA will establish an **LP Advisory Committee (LPAC)** to provide a forum for consultation between the General Partner and the limited partners on matters involving potential conflicts of interest, valuation issues, and other governance matters specified in the LPA.

**Composition.** The LPAC will consist of a minimum of **three (3)** and a maximum of **seven (7)** members, each of whom must be a representative of a limited partner in the Fund. Members will be selected by the General Partner from among the Fund\'s limited partners, with priority given to the largest limited partners and anchor investors. If non-U.S. commitments reach or exceed **\$50,000,000**, at least one LPAC member must be a representative of a non-U.S. limited partner, ensuring that the perspectives of non-U.S. investors are represented in the governance process.

**Functions.** The LPAC\'s functions, as specified in the LPA, will include:

> • **Consent to conflicts of interest.** The LPAC will be authorized to consent, on behalf of the limited partners, to transactions or arrangements that involve actual or potential conflicts of interest between the General Partner (or its affiliates) and the Fund, including co-investment allocations, cross-fund transactions, and related-party arrangements.
>
> • **Review of GP valuations.** The LPAC will review and provide input on the General Partner\'s valuations of portfolio company investments, particularly in connection with quarterly NAV calculations and the annual audit process.
>
> • **Approval of second fund extension.** While the General Partner may extend the Fund\'s term by one year at its discretion (from the initial ten-year term ending May 15, 2037 to May 15, 2038), the second one-year extension (from May 15, 2038 to May 15, 2039) requires the **consent of the LPAC**.
>
> • **Other matters.** The LPAC may be consulted on other matters specified in the LPA, including GP removal for cause, amendments to the LPA, and the formation of AIVs involving potential conflicts of interest.

**Anticipated Initial Members.** Based on the current investor pipeline, the anticipated initial LPAC members will include representatives of the Fund\'s anchor investors. **Ironwood PERS has specifically requested an advisory committee seat**, which we recommend granting given the size of Ironwood PERS\'s anticipated commitment (\$100 million) and its status as the Fund\'s largest expected limited partner. Representatives of Northgate and Pinnacle may also be invited to serve on the LPAC, depending on the final LPAC composition.

**LPAC Procedures.** The LPAC is an advisory body and does not have the authority to bind the Fund or the General Partner except as specifically provided in the LPA. LPAC members serve in their capacity as limited partners and do not owe fiduciary duties to the Fund or to other limited partners by virtue of their LPAC service. The LPA will include customary protections for LPAC members, including indemnification for actions taken in good faith in their LPAC capacity and release from liability for LPAC-approved transactions.

**[XII. TIMELINE AND NEXT STEPS]{.underline}**

**[XIII. CONCLUSION AND RECOMMENDATION]{.underline}**

Based on the analysis set forth in this memorandum, we recommend the following fund structure for Cobalt Life Sciences Opportunities Fund I:

**Core Structure:**

> • **Cobalt Life Sciences Opportunities Fund I, LP** --- a single-tier Delaware limited partnership serving as the primary fund vehicle.
>
> • **Cobalt Life Sciences GP I, LLC** --- a Delaware LLC serving as the General Partner, managed by Dr. Marcus Yeung and Priya Dasgupta, holding the carried interest entitlement (allocated Dr. Yeung 55%, Ms. Dasgupta 35%, Mr. Whitford 10%).
>
> • **Cobalt Life Sciences Management I, LLC** --- a Delaware LLC serving as the Management Company, employing the Fund\'s investment professionals and receiving the management fee.

**Ancillary Structures:**

> • **AIV Provisions** --- to be included in the LPA as a standard feature, authorizing the General Partner to form deal-specific or investor-specific alternative investment vehicles as needed to address tax, legal, regulatory, or operational requirements.

>
> • **Parallel Fund Enabling Provisions** --- to be included in the LPA, authorizing the General Partner to form a parallel fund without LP consent if non-U.S. investor demand reaches or exceeds \$50 million.
>
> • **Feeder Fund(s)** --- reserved as a future option, not currently planned. May be formed if fundraising dynamics warrant aggregation of smaller commitments.

> • **Master-Feeder Architecture** --- not recommended due to disproportionate cost and complexity relative to the predominantly U.S. domestic institutional investor base.
>
> • **Standalone Feeder Funds** --- not recommended for initial formation; reserved as a future option.

These structural recommendations remain available for reassessment if fundraising dynamics, investor demands, or regulatory developments change materially. filiates, partners, members, managers, officers, directors, and employees may engage in and possess interests in other business ventures and investment activities of any kind and description, including the management and operation of Fund IV and other investment funds, separately or jointly with others, whether or not competitive with the Partnership. No Limited Partner shall have any right to participate in, or receive any benefit from, any other investment opportunity of the General Partner, Ridgeline Management, or their Affiliates, except as may be expressly provided in a Side Letter.

**Section 7.7 --- Delegation**

The General Partner may delegate any of its powers, duties, and responsibilities hereunder to any officer, employee, agent, or Affiliate of the General Partner or Ridgeline Management; provided, however, that no such delegation shall relieve the General Partner of its obligations and liabilities under this Agreement or under the Act, and the General Partner shall remain fully responsible and liable for any act or omission of any delegate to the same extent as if such act or omission were the act or omission of the General Partner.

**Section 7.8 --- Standard of Care; Exculpation**

The General Partner shall manage the business and affairs of the Partnership in good faith and in a manner it reasonably believes to be in the best interests of the Partnership. No Covered Person shall be liable to the Partnership or to any Partner for any act or omission taken or suffered by such Covered Person in good faith and reasonably believed by such Covered Person to be in, or not opposed to, the best interests of the Partnership, provided that such act or omission does not constitute fraud, willful misconduct, bad faith, gross negligence, or a material breach of this Agreement. The General Partner shall not be liable for any error of judgment or for any mistake of fact or law. No Covered Person shall be obligated to guarantee the return of any Partner\'s Capital Contributions or a profit for any Partner from the operations of the Partnership.

**Section 7.9 --- Indemnification**

**(a) Scope of Indemnification.** To the fullest extent permitted by law, the Partnership shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless each Covered Person from and against any and all losses, damages, liabilities, claims, demands, actions, suits, proceedings, judgments, penalties, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys\' fees and expenses, court costs, and costs of investigation and settlement) (collectively, \"**Losses**\") incurred by such Covered Person and arising out of, resulting from, or in connection with (i) the business, operations, or affairs of the Partnership, (ii) such Covered Person\'s service to or on behalf of the Partnership, or (iii) such Covered Person\'s status as a Covered Person; provided, however, that the Partnership shall not indemnify any Covered Person for any Losses to the extent that such Losses arise from or are attributable to fraud, willful misconduct, bad faith, gross negligence, or a material breach of this Agreement by such Covered Person. The aggregate indemnification obligations of the Partnership under this Section 7.9 shall not exceed the total assets of the Partnership.

**(b) Advancement of Expenses.** The Partnership shall advance to any Covered Person reasonable expenses (including attorneys\' fees) incurred by such Covered Person in connection with any proceeding for which indemnification may be sought under this Section 7.9, upon receipt of a written undertaking by such Covered Person to repay such amounts to the Partnership if it is ultimately determined by a court of competent jurisdiction or by final arbitration award that such Covered Person is not entitled to indemnification under this Section 7.9.

**(c) Insurance.** The General Partner may, in its discretion, cause the Partnership to obtain and maintain directors\' and officers\' liability insurance, errors and omissions insurance, or such other insurance coverage as the General Partner deems appropriate to cover the Covered Persons with respect to their activities on behalf of the Partnership. The cost of any such insurance shall be an expense of the Partnership.

**[ARTICLE VIII --- TRANSFERS OF PARTNERSHIP INTERESTS]{.underline}**

**Section 8.1 --- Restrictions on Transfer**

No Limited Partner may Transfer all or any portion of its Partnership Interest without the prior written consent of the General Partner, which consent may be granted or withheld in the General Partner\'s sole and absolute discretion. As used herein, \"**Transfer**\" means any direct or indirect sale, assignment, transfer, conveyance, exchange, gift, pledge, hypothecation, encumbrance, or other disposition of all or any portion of a Partnership Interest or any economic or governance rights therein, whether voluntary or involuntary, by operation of law or otherwise, including by merger, consolidation, liquidation, dissolution, or similar transaction. Any attempted Transfer of a Partnership Interest in violation of this Article VIII shall be null and void and of no force or effect, and the Partnership shall not recognize any such Transfer or accord any rights hereunder to any purported transferee.

**Section 8.2 --- Conditions to Permitted Transfers**

Any Transfer of a Partnership Interest that is permitted by the General Partner pursuant to Section 8.1 shall be subject to and conditioned upon satisfaction of each of the following conditions:

\(a\) Compliance with the Right of First Refusal provisions set forth in Section 8.3;

\(b\) Receipt by the General Partner of a written opinion of counsel, satisfactory to the General Partner in form and substance and from counsel satisfactory to the General Partner, to the effect that such Transfer is exempt from registration under the Securities Act and under all applicable state securities laws;

\(c\) The proposed transferee shall execute and deliver to the General Partner a joinder agreement substantially in the form attached hereto as Exhibit A, pursuant to which such transferee agrees to be bound by all of the terms, conditions, and obligations of this Agreement applicable to the transferring Limited Partner;

\(d\) Such Transfer shall not cause the Partnership to be treated as a \"publicly traded partnership\" within the meaning of Section 7704 of the Code or otherwise to be taxable as a corporation for federal income tax purposes;

\(e\) The transferring Limited Partner shall pay, or cause to be paid, all reasonable out-of-pocket legal, accounting, and administrative costs and expenses incurred by the Partnership and the General Partner in connection with such Transfer; and

\(f\) Such Transfer shall not result in the Partnership being required to register as an investment company under the Investment Company Act of 1940; and

\(g\) Such other conditions as the General Partner may reasonably impose.

**Section 8.3 --- Right of First Refusal (ROFR)**

\(a\) Prior to any proposed Transfer of all or any portion of a Partnership Interest to any third party (other than a Permitted Transferee), the transferring Limited Partner shall deliver to the General Partner a written notice (a \"**Transfer Notice**\") setting forth (i) the identity of the proposed transferee, (ii) the proposed purchase price or other consideration for the Partnership Interest to be transferred, (iii) the material terms and conditions of the proposed Transfer, and (iv) a representation that the proposed Transfer complies with all applicable securities laws. A form of Transfer Notice is attached hereto as Exhibit C.

\(b\) The General Partner shall have a period of thirty (30) days following receipt of the Transfer Notice (the \"**GP ROFR Period**\") to elect, by written notice to the transferring Limited Partner, to purchase (or to cause any other Partner, Fund IV, or any other designee of the General Partner to purchase) all (but not less than all) of the Partnership Interest offered for Transfer, at the same price and on the same material terms and conditions set forth in the Transfer Notice.

\(c\) If the General Partner does not exercise the ROFR within the GP ROFR Period, the General Partner shall promptly notify the other Limited Partners, and the other Limited Partners shall have a further period of fifteen (15) days following receipt of such notice (the \"**LP ROFR Period**\") to elect, by written notice to the General Partner and the transferring Limited Partner, to purchase the offered Partnership Interest (or such portion thereof as is offered), pro rata based on their respective Partnership Percentages (calculated without regard to the transferring Limited Partner\'s Partnership Percentage). If more than one non-transferring Limited Partner elects to purchase and the aggregate elections exceed the offered Partnership Interest, such elections shall be satisfied pro rata based on the electing Limited Partners\' respective Partnership Percentages.

\(d\) If neither the General Partner nor the other Limited Partners exercise the ROFR within the applicable periods, the transferring Limited Partner may, subject to satisfaction of all other conditions in Section 8.2, consummate the Transfer to the proposed transferee identified in the Transfer Notice, at the same price and on terms no more favorable to the transferee than those set forth in the Transfer Notice, within ninety (90) days following the expiration of the LP ROFR Period. If the Transfer is not consummated within such ninety (90)-day period, the ROFR process set forth in this Section 8.3 must be repeated before any Transfer may occur.

**Section 8.4 --- Transfers by the General Partner**

The General Partner shall not Transfer its general partner interest in the Partnership without the prior written consent of Limited Partners holding a sixty-six and two-thirds percent (66⅔%) in interest of the aggregate Capital Commitments of all Limited Partners; provided, however, that the General Partner may, without the consent of the Limited Partners, Transfer its general partner interest to an Affiliate of the General Partner or Ridgeline Management, provided that (i) such Affiliate assumes all obligations of the General Partner hereunder, (ii) such Affiliate is wholly owned, directly or indirectly, by Ridgeline Management, and (iii) the General Partner provides at least ten (10) Business Days\' prior written notice to the Limited Partners of such Transfer.

**Section 8.5 --- Tag-Along Rights**

\(a\) If Fund IV, the GP, or any Affiliate of the GP or Ridgeline Management proposes to Transfer, directly or indirectly, all or any portion of any equity interest in AcquisitionCo to any Person (other than a Transfer to an Affiliate of the GP or Ridgeline Management) (a \"**Tag-Along Sale**\"), each Limited Partner shall have the right (a \"**Tag-Along Right**\") to participate in such Transfer on a pro rata basis, at the same price per unit of AcquisitionCo Equity and on the same terms and conditions as Fund IV. Each Limited Partner exercising its Tag-Along Right shall be entitled to receive the same form of consideration (whether cash, securities, or other property) as Fund IV, at the same price per unit and on the same terms and conditions, without any adverse adjustment.

\(b\) The General Partner shall provide at least twenty (20) Business Days\' prior written notice to each Limited Partner of any proposed Tag-Along Sale (a \"**Tag-Along Notice**\"), which notice shall set forth the identity of the proposed purchaser, the proposed price, and the material terms and conditions of the proposed sale.

\(c\) Each Limited Partner may elect to exercise its Tag-Along Right by delivering written notice to the General Partner within fifteen (15) Business Days of receipt of the Tag-Along Notice. Any Limited Partner that does not deliver a timely election notice shall be deemed to have waived its Tag-Along Right with respect to such Tag-Along Sale.

\(d\) Each Limited Partner exercising its Tag-Along Right may include in such Tag-Along Sale up to one hundred percent (100%) of its proportionate interest in the AcquisitionCo Equity (determined based on the Partnership\'s proportionate ownership of AcquisitionCo and such Limited Partner\'s Partnership Percentage).

\(e\) The closing of any Tag-Along Sale shall be conditioned upon the participation of all Limited Partners that have timely exercised their Tag-Along Rights.

\(f\) If the proposed transferee is unwilling to purchase the Partnership\'s (or the Limited Partners\') proportionate share, the Tag-Along Sale shall not proceed unless the GP obtains the prior written consent of a majority-in-interest of the Limited Partners.

**Section 8.6 --- Drag-Along Rights**

\(a\) If the General Partner determines, in its sole discretion, to sell one hundred percent (100%) of the AcquisitionCo Equity held by the Partnership and Fund IV to a third party (a \"**Drag-Along Sale**\"), the General Partner may require all Limited Partners to sell their proportionate interests in the AcquisitionCo Equity (indirectly, through the Partnership) on the same terms and conditions as Fund IV (the \"**Drag-Along Right**\"). The GP may exercise the Drag-Along Right only if the aggregate proceeds to be received by the Limited Partners in such Drag-Along Sale would result in each Limited Partner receiving, in the aggregate (including all prior distributions), at least a return of its Capital Contributions plus its Preferred Return Amount.

\(b\) The General Partner shall provide at least twenty (20) Business Days\' prior written notice to each Limited Partner of any proposed Drag-Along Sale (a \"**Drag-Along Notice**\"), which notice shall set forth the identity of the proposed purchaser, the proposed price, and the material terms and conditions of the proposed sale.

\(c\) In any Drag-Along Sale, each Limited Partner shall receive its proportionate share of the sale proceeds in accordance with the Distribution waterfall set forth in Section 6.2.

\(d\) In connection with any Drag-Along Sale, the representations and warranties required of the dragged Limited Partners shall be limited to (i) title to and ownership of their Partnership Interests, (ii) authority and power to enter into and perform the sale transaction, and (iii) the absence of encumbrances on their Partnership Interests. No Limited Partner shall be required to make any representations or warranties with respect to the business, assets, liabilities, operations, or financial condition of AcquisitionCo, Clarion, or any of their respective subsidiaries.

\(e\) Each Limited Partner hereby agrees to take all actions and execute all documents reasonably requested by the General Partner to consummate a Drag-Along Sale, including execution of purchase agreements, closing certificates, and related instruments.

\(f\) Any escrow, holdback, or indemnity obligations arising from a Drag-Along Sale shall be allocated pro rata among all equity holders (including Fund IV) based on their respective shares of proceeds.

**Section 8.7 --- Substitute Limited Partners**

A permitted transferee of a Partnership Interest shall be admitted to the Partnership as a substitute Limited Partner only upon satisfaction of all conditions set forth in Section 8.2 and execution and delivery of such documentation as the General Partner may reasonably require, including a joinder agreement substantially in the form of Exhibit A. Upon admission as a substitute Limited Partner, the transferee shall succeed to all of the rights and obligations of the transferring Limited Partner with respect to the transferred Partnership Interest, and the transferring Limited Partner shall be released from all obligations hereunder with respect to the transferred Partnership Interest (other than obligations that accrued prior to the effective date of such Transfer). The General Partner shall promptly update Schedule A to reflect any such substitution.

**[ARTICLE IX --- LIMITED PARTNER ADVISORY COMMITTEE (LPAC)]{.underline}**

**Section 9.1 --- Establishment and Composition**

The Partnership shall establish a Limited Partner Advisory Committee (the \"**LPAC**\") consisting of three (3) members. The members of the LPAC shall be appointed by the General Partner from among the Limited Partners or their designated representatives; provided, however, that Pellegrino Capital Group LLC shall be entitled to appoint one (1) member of the LPAC for so long as Pellegrino Capital Group LLC holds a Partnership Interest in the Partnership. LPAC members shall serve in a non-fiduciary, advisory capacity, except where specific approval or consent rights are expressly conferred upon the LPAC by this Agreement. For the avoidance of doubt, LPAC members shall not owe any fiduciary duties to the Partnership or to any other Partner by virtue of their service on the LPAC.

**Section 9.2 --- LPAC Functions**

The LPAC shall have the following functions and responsibilities:

\(a\) Review and approve (or disapprove) conflict transactions between the Partnership and the General Partner or any of its Affiliates as contemplated by Section 7.3(c);

\(b\) Review and approve (or disapprove) all other matters requiring LPAC consent as set forth in Section 7.3;

\(c\) Consult with the General Partner regarding valuations of the Investment, including the methodology and inputs used for such valuations;

\(d\) Review and approve (or disapprove) any proposed Distributions in kind pursuant to Section 6.7;

\(e\) Consult with the General Partner regarding the management transition plan in connection with a Key Person Event pursuant to Section 10.1; and

\(f\) Perform such other advisory functions as the General Partner may request from time to time, including review of the Partnership\'s annual financial statements and consultation on material strategic matters relating to the Investment ; and

\(g\) Review and consult on any proposed modification to the business plan or strategy of Clarion Hospitality Holdings, Inc. that would represent a material departure from the business plan presented to the Limited Partners in connection with their co-investment.

**Section 9.3 --- LPAC Meetings**

\(a\) The LPAC shall meet at least twice per calendar year, with at least one meeting to be held in person (which may be at the offices of the GP or such other location as the LPAC may agree), or more frequently as the General Partner or any two (2) LPAC members may request. Meetings may be held in person at the offices of the General Partner, by video conference, or by telephonic conference, as determined by the General Partner in consultation with the LPAC members.

\(b\) The General Partner shall provide at least ten (10) Business Days\' prior written notice of each meeting to all LPAC members, together with a written agenda and copies of any relevant materials to be discussed at such meeting.

\(c\) A quorum for any meeting of the LPAC shall consist of a majority of the LPAC members (i.e., two (2) of three (3) members). Actions of the LPAC shall be taken by the affirmative vote or written consent of a majority of the LPAC members (i.e., two (2) of three (3) members).

\(d\) Actions may be taken by the LPAC without a meeting by written consent signed by a majority of the LPAC members, which consent shall be effective as of the date of the last signature.

\(e\) The General Partner shall prepare and distribute to all LPAC members written minutes of each meeting within fifteen (15) Business Days following such meeting.

**Section 9.4 --- Indemnification of LPAC Members**

Each member of the LPAC shall be indemnified by the Partnership on the same basis as Covered Persons under Section 7.9 with respect to any Losses incurred by such member arising out of or in connection with such member\'s service on the LPAC. LPAC members acting in good faith in the performance of their duties as LPAC members shall have no personal liability to the Partnership, the General Partner, or any Limited Partner for any actions taken or omitted to be taken in their advisory capacity as LPAC members.

**Section 9.5 --- Removal and Replacement**

\(a\) The General Partner may remove any LPAC member for Cause upon written notice to such LPAC member and the Limited Partner that appointed or designated such member.

\(b\) Any Limited Partner that appointed or designated an LPAC member may, at any time, designate a replacement for such LPAC member by written notice to the General Partner, and such replacement shall become effective upon receipt of such notice by the General Partner.

\(c\) In the event of a vacancy on the LPAC (whether by removal, resignation, or otherwise), the General Partner shall appoint a replacement LPAC member from among the Limited Partners or their designated representatives within thirty (30) days of such vacancy; provided, however, that any vacancy in the LPAC seat held by a designee of Pellegrino Capital Group LLC shall be filled by a designee of Pellegrino Capital Group LLC.

**[ARTICLE X --- KEY PERSON; EXCUSE RIGHTS]{.underline}**

**Section 10.1 --- Key Person Provisions**

**(a) Key Persons.** The Key Persons are Julian T. Whitmore (Co-Founder & Managing Partner, Ridgeline Equity Management LLC) and Connor M. Rafferty (Partner, Head of Hospitality, Ridgeline Equity Management LLC). The Limited Partners have entered into this Agreement in reliance upon the active involvement of the Key Persons in the management and oversight of the Investment.

**(b) Key Person Event.** A \"**Key Person Event**\" shall occur if either Key Person ceases to be actively involved in the management and oversight of the Investment and the business of Fund IV as it relates to the hospitality sector. For purposes of this Section 10.1, \"active involvement\" requires that each Key Person devotes a minimum of sixty percent (60%) of such individual\'s professional time and attention to Fund IV, the Partnership, and related investment activities. A Key Person Event shall be triggered by the departure or reduction in active involvement of either Key Person, given the concentrated, single-asset nature of the co-investment and the importance of both Key Persons to the hospitality investment thesis.

The proposed Engagement would encompass the following matters: (a) serving as primary fund formation counsel for Harrowgate Private Equity Fund V LP, a Delaware limited partnership to be formed (the "Fund"); (b) drafting and negotiating the Amended and Restated Agreement of Limited Partnership of the Fund (the "Limited Partnership Agreement" or "LPA"); (c) preparing the Confidential Private Placement Memorandum (the "PPM") and related disclosure documents; (d) preparing subscription agreements, investor questionnaires, and all ancillary subscription documentation; (e) preparing all formation and organizational documents for the Fund and related entities; (f) providing tax structuring advice in connection with the formation and operation of parallel and feeder vehicles, including Harrowgate Fund V Parallel LP (a Delaware limited partnership), Harrowgate Fund V Offshore SLP (a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership), and HGF V blocker Corp. (a Delaware C corporation); (g) negotiating side letters with prospective anchor limited partners and their respective counsel; (h) reviewing and advising on the placement agent agreement, fund administration agreement, subscription credit facility documentation, custody agreement, and auditor engagement letter; and (i) providing regulatory advice in connection with Regulation D and other applicable securities law exemptions, as well as ERISA, Bank Secrecy Act / AML, and CFIUS considerations as relevant to the investor base.

In the course of a private fund formation and fundraise, the Firm will negotiate the LPA, side letters, and related documentation with counsel retained by prospective anchor limited partners. The following law firms have been identified as counsel to prospective anchor LPs in the Fund and were screened through the C&H Conflicts System to confirm that no conflicts of interest exist. Calderwood & Harkness LLP does not represent any of these firms in any capacity, has no pending adverse matters involving any of these firms, and has no attorney currently associated with the Firm who has a personal or financial interest in any of these firms.

•  Role in Transaction: Lead investor-side counsel in the fundraise; responsible for negotiating side letter terms and LPA provisions on behalf of Northmoor State Pension System. Expected to be the most active LP counsel in the first close process.
•  Role in Transaction: Investor-side counsel representing The Kingsbridge Endowment Fund in negotiating LPA terms, side letter provisions, and blocker structure considerations.

•  Role in Transaction: Investor-side counsel representing Tidewater Sovereign Investment Authority in negotiating LPA terms, side letter provisions, offshore feeder structuring, CFIUS-related representations, and sovereign immunity considerations.

Supplemental Screening Policy. In accordance with the Firm's standard policy for fund formation engagements, if additional prospective limited partners, co-investors, or other counterparties are identified after the date of this memorandum—whether during the fundraise process, at subsequent closes, or otherwise during the course of the Engagement—supplemental conflict checks will be run against such parties prior to any substantive engagement with them. The billing partner (Pamela Cross) and the deal team leads (Stephen Adler and Theresa Kim) have been advised of this ongoing obligation and will submit supplemental conflict check requests to the Conflicts Department as new parties are identified throughout the fundraise.

Although no conflicts of interest have been identified, the following analysis addresses the categories of potential conflict issues that are customarily considered in connection with a private fund formation engagement of this nature.

Dual Representation / Multiple-Client Issues. Calderwood & Harkness LLP will represent only Harrowgate Capital Partners LLC and the Fund entities (i.e., Harrowgate Private Equity Fund V LP, Harrowgate Fund V GP LLC, Harrowgate Fund V Parallel LP, Harrowgate Fund V Offshore SLP, and HGF V blocker Corp.) in its capacity as issuer's counsel and fund formation counsel. The Firm will not represent any limited partner in connection with the Fund or in any related matter. Each of the anchor limited partners identified in Section III.A above has retained, or is expected to retain, independent legal counsel for the purpose of reviewing and negotiating the terms of the LPA, the PPM, the subscription documents, and any applicable side letters. There is no dual representation issue, and no informed consent from any limited partner is required under the applicable Rules of Professional Conduct.

To the extent that the interests of the General Partner and the Fund (as an entity distinct from its General Partner) could theoretically diverge on certain terms—such as management fee calculations, carried interest waterfalls, GP clawback provisions, removal-for-cause provisions, or key person event triggers—such alignment-of-interest issues are inherent in virtually all fund formation representations and are customarily managed through disclosure in the engagement letter and the PPM. The engagement letter will contain appropriate language identifying the Client as Harrowgate Capital Partners LLC (together with its controlled affiliates forming the Fund structure) and clarifying that the Firm's duty of loyalty runs to HCP as the Sponsor and that the Firm does not independently represent the interests of the limited partners.

Adverse Party Considerations. In the ordinary course of the fundraise, Calderwood & Harkness LLP will negotiate side letter provisions and LPA terms with investor-side counsel, including Aldworth & McBride LLP (counsel to Northmoor State Pension System), Pelham Chambers LLP (counsel to The Kingsbridge Endowment Fund), and Ramsden Clarke International LLP (counsel to Tidewater Sovereign Investment Authority). This negotiation is a customary and expected feature of private fund formation practice and does not create an adverse-party conflict under applicable rules. The prospective limited partners are not "adverse parties" to the Client within the meaning of the Model Rules of Professional Conduct or the Delaware Lawyers' Rules of Professional Conduct; rather, they are prospective investors whose interests are substantially aligned with those of the Sponsor in the successful formation and operation of the Fund, notwithstanding the fact that certain economic and governance terms will be subject to negotiation. This analysis is consistent with the prevailing interpretation of Rule 1.7 in the fund formation context, including ABA Formal Ethics Opinion 08-451 and applicable state bar guidance.

Third-Party Service Providers. The Fund's engagement of Osprey Capital Markets LLC (placement agent), Pinnacle Fund Services LLC (fund administrator), Caldwell, Fitch & Hartley LLP (independent auditor), Ashford National Bank, N.A. (subscription credit facility lender), and Ridgeway Trust Company (custodian) does not create any conflict of interest for the Firm. Calderwood & Harkness LLP will review, negotiate, and advise the Client on certain agreements with these service providers on behalf of the Client, which constitutes standard transactional and advisory work in the fund formation context. The Firm does not represent any of these service providers, and its role as counsel to the Client in negotiating the terms of the relevant agreements (e.g., the placement agent agreement, the administration agreement, the credit facility documentation, the custody agreement, and the auditor engagement letter) is fully consistent with the Firm's duties to the Client.

Conclusion. Based on the comprehensive search conducted on March 31 and April 1, 2025, including the screening of all client entities, client personnel, prospective anchor limited partners, third-party service providers, counterparty counsel, and prior employer cross-references as described in this memorandum, no conflicts of interest have been identified that would preclude Calderwood & Harkness LLP from accepting the proposed Engagement to serve as fund formation counsel to Harrowgate Capital Partners LLC in connection with the formation and fundraise of Harrowgate Private Equity Fund V LP, Harrowgate Fund V Parallel LP, Harrowgate Fund V Offshore SLP, HGF V blocker Corp., and related vehicles.

Description. This workstream covers the preparation of the limited partnership agreements for two parallel investment vehicles designed to accommodate the structural requirements of certain categories of investors:

Parallel Fund. The Parallel Fund will be structured as a Delaware limited partnership (Harrowgate Private Equity Fund V Parallel LP) for certain tax-exempt and non-U.S. limited partners requiring structural separation from the Main Fund for tax, regulatory, or reporting reasons. Offshore Feeder. The Offshore Feeder will be structured as a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership (Harrowgate Private Equity Fund V Offshore LP) for non-U.S. investors, including in particular the Tidewater Sovereign Investment Authority, which has indicated an anticipated commitment of $175,000,000 through this vehicle. The Offshore Feeder will invest substantially all of its assets as a limited partner in the Main Fund (or the Parallel Fund, as applicable), thereby ensuring economic parity across the fund complex.

Analysis under Rule 1.9 (Former Client): Under California Rule of Professional Conduct 1.9(a), a lawyer who has formerly represented a client in a matter shall not thereafter represent another person in the same or a substantially related matter in which that person's interests are materially adverse to the interests of the former client unless the former client gives informed written consent. The key inquiry is whether the proposed patent infringement litigation on behalf of OWS against Lumos Photonics is the "same or substantially related matter" as the prior transactional representation of the GP entity in connection with the Fund III limited partnership agreement amendment.

The proposed engagement involves the prosecution of a patent infringement action in the semiconductor and silicon photonics technology space. There is no factual overlap, no common legal issues, and no common subject matter between the two engagements. The Fund is governed by its Amended and Restated Limited Partnership Agreement dated March 15, 2017 (as amended from time to time, the "A&R LPA"), which is governed by the laws of the State of Delaware. The A&R LPA provides for certain key-person protections in favor of the Fund's limited partners, as more fully described in Section 3 below.

This engagement is precipitated by the medical incapacitation of Marcus J. Whitmore, Founder, Chief Investment Officer, and Managing Member (holding a ninety percent (90%) membership interest) of DCM. Mr. Whitmore suffered a severe hemorrhagic stroke on June 3, 2024, and has been incapacitated since that date. Mr. Whitmore is the sole individual designated as a "Key Person" under Section 8.04(a) of the A&R LPA. As a result of Mr. Whitmore's continued incapacitation for a period exceeding seven consecutive calendar days from the date of the medical event, a Key Person Event under Section 8.04(b) of the A&R LPA is deemed to have been triggered as of June 10, 2024 (the "Key Person Event"). The occurrence of the Key Person Event gives rise to a number of contractual obligations, rights, and remedies under the A&R LPA that require prompt legal attention and careful navigation by DCM in its capacity as General Partner of the Fund.

This engagement letter confirms the terms and conditions under which C&H will provide legal advisory services to the Clients (as defined below) in connection with the Key Person Event, including, without limitation, analysis of the A&R LPA's key-person provisions, preparation of required limited partner notifications, development of a successor governance framework, drafting of LPA amendments, and coordination of the limited partner consent solicitation process.

C&H's representation of the Clients will encompass the following workstreams in connection with the Key Person Event triggered under Section 8.04 of the A&R LPA. Each workstream is described in further detail below.
C&H will undertake a comprehensive analysis of the mechanics and consequences of Section 8.04 of the A&R LPA, including the following:

(a) Section 8.04(a) — Definition of "Key Person." C&H will confirm the scope of the "Key Person" designation under the A&R LPA, which identifies Marcus J. Whitmore as the sole designated Key Person. C&H will analyze the definition for purposes of establishing the factual predicate for the Key Person Event and for advising on the requirements for designating any Successor Key Person(s) (as described in Section 3.3 below).

(b) Section 8.04(b) — Trigger Conditions. C&H will analyze the trigger conditions set forth in Section 8.04(b) of the A&R LPA in light of the facts surrounding Mr. Whitmore's incapacitation. Specifically, Section 8.04(b) provides that a Key Person Event is deemed to occur when the Key Person becomes unable, whether by reason of death, disability, incapacity, departure, or otherwise, to devote substantially all of his professional time and attention to the affairs of the Fund for a period of seven (7) consecutive calendar days. Based on the information provided to C&H, Mr. Whitmore has been continuously incapacitated since June 3, 2024, and the seven-consecutive-calendar-day threshold was met as of June 10, 2024. C&H will prepare a memorandum confirming the legal basis for this determination.

(c) Section 8.04(c) — Consequences of the Key Person Event. C&H will advise the Clients regarding the full range of consequences triggered by the occurrence of the Key Person Event under Section 8.04(c) of the A&R LPA, which include the following:

(i) Immediate Suspension of the Investment Period. The Investment Period (as defined in Section 1.01 of the A&R LPA) is automatically suspended upon the occurrence of a Key Person Event. During such suspension, the General Partner may not make new portfolio investments on behalf of the Fund, except as provided in clause (ii) below.

(d) Consequences of Failure to Cure. C&H will further analyze the consequences under Section 8.04(d) of the A&R LPA if no cure is achieved within the Cure Period, including the limited partners' right to elect, by the same 66⅔% consent threshold described above, either (x) to extend the Cure Period for one or more additional periods or (y) to direct the General Partner to commence an orderly wind-down of the Fund's portfolio. C&H will advise the Clients on the mechanics, timing, and fiduciary considerations associated with each of these alternatives.

(e) Delaware Law Fiduciary Duty Analysis. C&H will advise the Clients regarding the fiduciary duties owed by DCM, as General Partner, to the limited partners of the Fund during the Key Person Event and throughout the consent solicitation process, as a matter of Delaware law. This analysis will address, among other things, the duty of care and the contractual modification of fiduciary duties under the A&R LPA, including the exculpation and indemnification provisions set forth in Article XII thereof.

C&H will draft the formal written notice to all forty-seven (47) limited partners of the Fund disclosing the occurrence of the Key Person Event in compliance with Section 8.04(c) of the A&R LPA (the "Key Person Notice"). The Key Person Notice will describe the factual basis for the Key Person Event, the contractual consequences thereof, the commencement and expected expiration date of the Cure Period, and the process by which the General Partner intends to propose Successor Key Person(s) for approval by the limited partners.

C&H will coordinate with Pinnacle Fund Services (Cayman) Ltd. (the "Administrator"), the Fund's third-party administrator, regarding the maintenance and accuracy of LP contact information, the appropriate method of delivery (including any notice provisions specified in the A&R LPA or in individual side letters), and the mechanics of distributing the Key Person Notice to all limited partners within the contractual timeframe. C&H will confirm with the Administrator that notice is delivered by a method that satisfies the delivery requirements of Section 15.01 of the A&R LPA.

(a) Designation of Successor Key Person(s). C&H will advise on the criteria and process for designating one or more Successor Key Persons under the A&R LPA, including the qualifications, investment experience, and operational capabilities that limited partners are likely to consider in evaluating any proposed successor. C&H will assist in preparing biographical and professional materials for inclusion in the consent solicitation package.

(b) Establishment of an Investment Committee. In the event that the Clients determine that the successor governance framework should include the establishment of a formal Investment Committee or similar collective governance body (in lieu of, or in addition to, a sole Key Person designation), C&H will advise on the structure, composition, authority, and operating procedures of such body, and will prepare the necessary amendments to the A&R LPA to implement such structure.

(c) Modifications to Key-Person Clause Mechanics. C&H will advise on potential modifications to the key-person provisions of Section 8.04 of the A&R LPA, which may include revised replacement periods, modified trigger events (including, for example, a threshold requiring the departure or incapacitation of more than one designated Key Person before a Key Person Event is deemed to occur), and other structural changes to reduce single-person dependency risk.

(d) Carried Interest Reallocation. C&H will advise the Clients on the legal and governance considerations associated with any proposed reallocation of carried interest among GP personnel in connection with the transition, including the interplay between the carried interest provisions of the A&R LPA and the operating agreement of DCM.
3.4 LPA Amendment Drafting

C&H will prepare one or more amendments to the A&R LPA (each, an "LPA Amendment") to implement the successor governance framework developed pursuant to Section 3.3 above. It is anticipated that the LPA Amendments will include modifications to the following provisions of the A&R LPA, among others:
(d) Related schedules and exhibits, including the schedule of Key Persons attached to the A&R LPA.

All LPA Amendments will be subject to the consent requirements set forth in Section 14.01 of the A&R LPA, which generally requires the written consent of the General Partner and limited partners holding at least 66⅔% of aggregate LP capital commitments (excluding GP co-investment) for amendments to certain specified provisions, including Section 8.04. C&H will advise the Clients regarding the applicable consent thresholds for each proposed amendment.

C&H will advise on and coordinate the consent solicitation process necessary to obtain limited partner approval of the proposed Successor Key Person(s) and the related LPA Amendments. This workstream will include the following:

(a) Successor Key Person Proposal Letter. C&H will draft a detailed letter to all limited partners setting forth the proposed Successor Key Person(s), the rationale for the proposed designation(s), the terms of the proposed successor governance framework, and a summary of the proposed LPA Amendments (the "Proposal Letter"). The Proposal Letter will be designed to provide limited partners with all information reasonably necessary to make an informed decision regarding the proposed successor arrangements.

(b) Form of LP Written Consent. C&H will prepare a Form of LP Written Consent (the "Consent Form") for execution by limited partners approving the proposed Successor Key Person(s) and the related LPA Amendments. The Consent Form will be structured to comply with the requirements of Section 14.01 and Section 8.04(c) of the A&R LPA.

(d) Tabulation and Certification. C&H will tabulate the LP consents received and prepare a closing certificate confirming that the requisite consent threshold (66⅔% of aggregate LP capital commitments, excluding GP co-investment) has been satisfied and that the LPA Amendments are effective as of the date specified therein (the "Closing Certificate").

(e) Engagement with IAC Counsel. C&H will engage with counsel to the Investor Advisory Committee, Wexford Crane & Albright LLP, as necessary and appropriate regarding the IAC's review of and comments on the proposed Successor Key Person(s), the successor governance framework, and the LPA Amendments. C&H will coordinate with the Clients regarding any modifications to the proposed arrangements that may be requested by the IAC or its counsel.

For the avoidance of doubt, the A&R LPA is governed by the laws of the State of Delaware, and C&H's analysis and advice rendered under this engagement with respect to the interpretation and enforcement of the provisions of the A&R LPA, including Section 8.04 and the fiduciary duties of the General Partner, will apply the substantive law of the State of Delaware. Nothing in this Section 7 is intended to alter the governing law of the A&R LPA or any other agreement to which the Clients are a party.
(a) Review and analysis of the Limited Partnership Agreement of Meridian Peak Capital Partners Fund IV, L.P. (the "Fund IV LPA"), including all schedules, exhibits, and amendments thereto;

A positional conflict may arise where a law firm simultaneously represents clients whose legal positions are materially adverse to one another, even if the clients are not direct adversaries in the same matter. In the fund formation context, a positional conflict could arise if, for example, the Firm were simultaneously representing both the fund sponsor (on the fund-formation side) and an investor seeking favorable side-letter terms from that same sponsor.

Ms. Kim will serve as BFO's primary point of contact for routine matters and status updates.
•  LPA/PPM review and analysis: approximately $30,000 – $40,000

BFO further acknowledges that the existence and terms of the Side Letter may be subject to confidentiality restrictions under the LPA and the Side Letter itself, and that C&H's ability to reference the terms of the Side Letter in future matters may be limited by such restrictions.
