**[LIMITED PARTNER ADVISORY COMMITTEE CHARTER AND TERMS OF REFERENCE]{.underline}**

**HARROWGATE PRIVATE EQUITY FUND V LP** a Delaware limited partnership (the \"Fund\")

**General Partner:** Harrowgate Fund V GP LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (the \"General Partner\"), whose sole member is Harrowgate Capital Partners LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (the \"Sponsor\")

**Effective as of the date of the First Close** (Target: August 15, 2025)

This Limited Partner Advisory Committee Charter and Terms of Reference (this \"Charter\") is adopted by the General Partner of Harrowgate Private Equity Fund V LP, a Delaware limited partnership, pursuant to Section 11.1 of the Agreement of Limited Partnership of Harrowgate Private Equity Fund V LP, dated as of August 15, 2025 (as amended, restated, supplemented, or otherwise modified from time to time, the \"Partnership Agreement\" or \"LPA\").

Capitalized terms used but not defined herein shall have the meanings given to them in the Partnership Agreement. This Charter shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to its conflicts of law principles.

Right-click to update Table of Contents

**[ARTICLE I --- PURPOSE AND ESTABLISHMENT]{.underline}**

**Section 1.1 --- Establishment of the LPAC**

The General Partner hereby establishes a Limited Partner Advisory Committee (the \"LPAC\" or the \"Committee\") for Harrowgate Private Equity Fund V LP. The LPAC is established to serve in a consultative and advisory capacity to the General Partner on certain matters as set forth herein and in the Partnership Agreement, and to foster transparency and constructive dialogue between the General Partner and the Fund\'s Limited Partners regarding Fund governance, potential conflicts of interest, and other matters of significance to the Fund\'s investor base.

The LPAC is not a governing body of the Fund and does not have the authority to manage, control, or direct the business and affairs of the Fund, which authority is vested exclusively in the General Partner pursuant to the Partnership Agreement and applicable Delaware law, including the Delaware Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act (6 Del. C. §§ 17-101 *et seq.*). The establishment of the LPAC shall not alter or diminish the powers and authority of the General Partner as set forth in the Partnership Agreement or give rise to any inference that the LPAC exercises control over, or participates in the control of, the Fund\'s business.

**Section 1.2 --- Purpose**

The LPAC is established for the following purposes:

> \(a\) To review and, where required by the Partnership Agreement, approve or consent to certain transactions and matters involving actual or potential conflicts of interest between the General Partner (or its affiliates, principals, or related persons) and the Fund or the Limited Partners;
>
> \(b\) To consult on valuation matters referred to it by the General Partner, including the review of valuation methodologies and conclusions presented by the General Partner on at least an annual basis;
>
> \(c\) To approve or consent to certain waivers of investment restrictions and guidelines as set forth in the Partnership Agreement, upon the request of the General Partner;
>
> \(d\) To approve or consent to extensions of the Fund Term beyond those that the General Partner is entitled to effect at its sole discretion under the Partnership Agreement;
>
> \(e\) To serve as a forum for communication and consultation between the General Partner and the Limited Partners on matters of Fund governance, operations, fees and expenses, and such other matters as the General Partner may, in its discretion, bring before the LPAC; and
>
> \(f\) To perform such other advisory functions as are contemplated by the Partnership Agreement or this Charter.

For the avoidance of doubt, the LPAC\'s role is advisory and consultative in nature, except where the Partnership Agreement expressly requires the LPAC\'s approval or consent as a condition to the General Partner taking or refraining from taking a specified action. Fiduciary duties do not attach to LPAC Members in their capacity as such, and LPAC Members shall not be deemed to be agents, trustees, or fiduciaries of the Fund, the General Partner, or any other Limited Partner by reason of their service on the LPAC.

**[ARTICLE II --- COMPOSITION AND MEMBERSHIP]{.underline}**

**Section 2.1 --- Number of Members**

The LPAC shall consist of five (5) members (each, a \"Member\" and, collectively, the \"Members\"). Three (3) Members shall be designated at the First Close of the Fund. The remaining two (2) Members shall be designated by the General Partner, in consultation with the existing Members, at subsequent closings or as vacancies arise, but in any event no later than the Final Close Deadline (February 15, 2027). In the period between the First Close and the designation of the fourth and fifth Members, the LPAC shall function with three (3) Members, and all quorum and voting thresholds shall be adjusted accordingly as set forth in Article III.

**Section 2.2 --- Initial Members**

The following Limited Partners (or their designated representatives) are anticipated to be designated as the initial three (3) Members of the LPAC at the First Close:

> \(a\) **Northmoor State Pension System** (anticipated capital commitment: \$200,000,000) --- designated representative: Helen T. Barrows, Director of Private Markets;
>
> \(b\) **Edgecombe Insurance Group Ltd.** (anticipated capital commitment: \$150,000,000) --- designated representative: Alastair G. Dunmore, Head of Alternative Investments; and
>
> \(c\) **The Kingsbridge Endowment Fund** (anticipated capital commitment: \$100,000,000) --- designated representative: Dr. Philip W. Sheng, Chief Investment Officer.

Each initial Member\'s appointment to the LPAC is subject to confirmation upon such Member\'s execution and delivery of its respective Subscription Agreement and any applicable Side Letter to the General Partner. In the event that any anticipated initial Member does not execute a Subscription Agreement at or prior to the First Close, the General Partner shall designate a replacement Member from among the Limited Partners admitted at the First Close.

**Section 2.3 --- Selection Criteria**

Members shall be selected from among Limited Partners with meaningful capital commitments to the Fund. In selecting Members, the General Partner shall endeavor to maintain a diverse and representative LPAC that reflects the breadth and composition of the Fund\'s investor base, including, as applicable, representation from among pension plans, endowments and foundations, insurance companies, sovereign wealth funds, funds of funds, family offices, and other institutional investors.

LPAC membership is available to investors in the Main Fund (Harrowgate Private Equity Fund V LP), the Parallel Fund (Harrowgate Fund V Parallel LP), and the Offshore Feeder (Harrowgate Fund V Offshore SLP), as each such vehicle invests alongside the Main Fund on a pro rata basis and participates in the same investment program. A Limited Partner\'s membership in the LPAC shall not be conditioned upon its investment through any particular vehicle within the fund complex.

**Section 2.4 --- Observer Status**

The General Partner may, in its sole discretion, grant observer status to one or more Limited Partners, permitting such Limited Partners (through their designated representatives) to attend LPAC meetings in a non-voting, advisory capacity. Observers shall not be counted for purposes of determining a quorum and shall not have the right to vote on any matter presented to the LPAC, but may participate in discussions at the invitation of the General Partner or the Members. Observers shall be bound by the same confidentiality obligations applicable to Members as set forth in Article VII of this Charter.

The General Partner acknowledges that certain Side Letters may provide for LPAC observer rights. By way of example, the Tidewater Sovereign Investment Authority has been granted LPAC observer rights pursuant to its negotiated Side Letter, and such rights shall be honored in accordance with the terms thereof, subject to the confidentiality and other provisions of this Charter.

**Section 2.5 --- Designated Representatives**

Each Member shall designate one (1) individual to serve as its representative on the LPAC (the \"Designated Representative\") and one (1) alternate representative (the \"Alternate Representative\"). The Designated Representative shall be the primary attendee at LPAC meetings and shall have full authority to act and vote on behalf of such Member. In the absence or unavailability of the Designated Representative, the Alternate Representative shall be entitled to attend and participate in meetings and to cast votes on behalf of such Member with the same authority as the Designated Representative.

All designations and changes of Designated Representatives and Alternate Representatives shall be communicated in writing (including by email) to the General Partner, to the attention of Rachel M. Overton, Partner, Head of Investor Relations, Harrowgate Capital Partners LLC, and shall be effective upon receipt by the General Partner. The General Partner shall maintain a current register of Designated Representatives and Alternate Representatives.

**Section 2.6 --- Term of Membership**

Each Member shall serve on the LPAC for the duration of the Fund Term (including any extension thereof), unless such Member earlier resigns, is removed, or ceases to be a Limited Partner in the Fund (including by reason of a full transfer of its limited partnership interest in the Fund). A Member that transfers all of its limited partnership interest in the Fund (whether pursuant to a secondary sale or otherwise) shall automatically cease to be a Member of the LPAC effective as of the date of such transfer, without the necessity of any further action by the General Partner or the LPAC.

A Member that transfers a portion, but not all, of its limited partnership interest in the Fund shall retain its LPAC membership, provided that such Member continues to hold a limited partnership interest in the Fund following such partial transfer.

**Section 2.7 --- Resignation and Removal**

> \(a\) **Resignation.** A Member may resign from the LPAC at any time by delivering written notice of resignation to the General Partner. Such resignation shall be effective upon receipt by the General Partner or such later date as may be specified in the notice.
>
> \(b\) **Removal.** The General Partner may replace a Member upon the occurrence of any of the following events:
>
> \(i\) such Member ceases to hold any limited partnership interest in the Fund (including by reason of a full transfer of its interest);
>
> \(ii\) such Member becomes subject to a Bankruptcy Event (as defined in the Partnership Agreement);
>
> \(iii\) such Member (or its Designated Representative or Alternate Representative) fails to attend three (3) consecutive regularly scheduled meetings of the LPAC without designating an alternate or otherwise providing prior notice of non-attendance to the General Partner; or
>
> \(iv\) such Member materially breaches its confidentiality obligations under Article VII of this Charter and fails to cure such breach within thirty (30) days following written notice from the General Partner specifying the nature of such breach.
>
> \(c\) **Process.** Replacement Members shall be selected by the General Partner in consultation with the remaining LPAC Members. The General Partner shall use commercially reasonable efforts to ensure that the composition of the LPAC continues to satisfy the diversity and representativeness objectives set forth in Section 2.3.

**Section 2.8 --- Vacancies**

Vacancies on the LPAC arising from resignation, removal, or any other cause shall be filled by the General Partner after consultation with the existing Members. The General Partner shall endeavor to fill any vacancy within sixty (60) days of the date on which such vacancy arises. During any period in which a vacancy exists and the remaining number of Members is fewer than five (5), the LPAC shall continue to function, and quorum and voting thresholds shall be determined by reference to the number of Members then serving.

**[ARTICLE III --- MEETINGS]{.underline}**

**Section 3.1 --- Frequency**

The LPAC shall meet at least two (2) times per calendar year at such times as the General Partner shall determine. Additional meetings may be called by the General Partner at any time, or upon the written request of at least two (2) Members specifying the purpose of the requested meeting. The General Partner shall use commercially reasonable efforts to schedule meetings at times that accommodate the schedules of the Members. The General Partner\'s principal contact for LPAC coordination and scheduling shall be Rachel M. Overton, Partner, Head of Investor Relations, Harrowgate Capital Partners LLC (email: r.overton@harrowgatecapital.com; telephone: (302) 555-1200).

**Section 3.2 --- Notice**

The General Partner shall provide not less than fifteen (15) business days\' prior written notice of each regularly scheduled meeting and not less than five (5) business days\' prior written notice of each special meeting. Each notice of meeting shall include a proposed agenda, the date, time, and location (or videoconference/teleconference dial-in information) of the meeting, and any materials to be considered at the meeting. Notice may be delivered by email to each Member\'s Designated Representative (and Alternate Representative) at the email address on file with the General Partner.

In the event of exigent circumstances requiring urgent LPAC action (for example, a time-sensitive conflict-of-interest transaction), the General Partner may provide shorter notice, provided that the General Partner uses commercially reasonable efforts to provide as much advance notice as is practicable under the circumstances and that no fewer than two (2) business days\' notice is given.

**Section 3.3 --- Format**

Meetings of the LPAC may be held in person at the offices of Harrowgate Capital Partners LLC at 1200 Concord Pike, Suite 600, Wilmington, Delaware 19803, or at such other location as designated by the General Partner, or by teleconference or videoconference, or any combination thereof. Members may participate in any meeting by means of conference telephone, video conferencing platform (e.g., Calderon Software, Northgate Data Systems), or similar communications equipment that allows all participants to hear each other at the same time, and such participation shall constitute presence in person at such meeting for all purposes under this Charter.

The General Partner shall make reasonable accommodations for Members located in different time zones, including, without limitation, by rotating meeting times or scheduling meetings during business hours that are reasonably convenient for Members in multiple jurisdictions.

**Section 3.4 --- Quorum**

A quorum for the transaction of business at any meeting of the LPAC shall consist of a majority of the Members then serving. By way of illustration, when all five (5) seats on the LPAC are filled, a quorum shall consist of three (3) Members; when only three (3) seats are filled (as may be the case between the First Close and the designation of the fourth and fifth Members), a quorum shall consist of two (2) Members. For purposes of determining a quorum, a Member shall be deemed present if the Member\'s Designated Representative or Alternate Representative is in attendance (whether in person, by teleconference, or by videoconference). Observers shall not be counted for purposes of determining a quorum.

No action may be taken at a meeting at which a quorum is not present, except to adjourn the meeting to a later date. In the event a quorum is not present, the Members present may adjourn the meeting to a date not more than fifteen (15) business days later, and the General Partner shall provide notice of such adjourned meeting to all Members not in attendance.

**Section 3.5 --- Voting and Action**

Each Member shall have one (1) vote on each matter submitted to the LPAC for a vote, regardless of the size of such Member\'s capital commitment to the Fund. Except as otherwise expressly provided herein or in the Partnership Agreement, actions of the LPAC shall require the affirmative vote of a majority of the Members present at a meeting at which a quorum is constituted.

Action may be taken by the LPAC without a meeting by unanimous written consent, circulated by the General Partner and executed (including by electronic signature or email confirmation) by all Members then serving. Any action so taken shall have the same force and effect as if taken at a duly convened meeting of the LPAC. The General Partner shall retain the original or electronic copies of all written consents in the Fund\'s records.

In the event of a tie vote (which may occur if the LPAC has an even number of Members then serving due to a vacancy), the matter in question shall be deemed not approved, and the General Partner may request that the matter be reconsidered at a subsequent meeting or by written consent.

**Section 3.6 --- Agenda and Materials**

The General Partner shall prepare and circulate the agenda for each meeting of the LPAC together with the notice of such meeting. Any Member may request that items be added to the agenda by written notice to the General Partner delivered at least five (5) business days before the meeting. The General Partner shall use reasonable efforts to accommodate such requests but reserves the right to defer items to a subsequent meeting if, in the General Partner\'s reasonable judgment, the requested item is not time-sensitive or if adequate materials cannot be prepared in advance.

The General Partner shall provide Members with relevant materials in advance of the meeting, including, as applicable, conflict-of-interest descriptions and analyses, valuation reports and summaries, supporting documentation for any matter requiring LPAC approval or consent, portfolio summaries, fee and expense reports, and such other information as the General Partner deems appropriate or as any Member may reasonably request. To the extent practicable, materials shall be provided at least five (5) business days in advance of the meeting to afford Members adequate time for review.

**Section 3.7 --- Minutes**

The General Partner (or its designee) shall prepare minutes of each meeting of the LPAC. Minutes shall include a summary of the matters discussed, the text of any resolutions adopted, the vote of each Member on each matter submitted to a vote, and a record of attendance. Draft minutes shall be circulated to all Members who attended the meeting for review within twenty (20) business days following the meeting. Members shall have ten (10) business days from receipt of draft minutes to submit comments or corrections. Minutes shall be finalized upon the approval of a majority of the Members who attended the meeting to which the minutes relate. Finalized minutes shall be maintained by the General Partner as part of the Fund\'s books and records.

**Section 3.8 --- Attendance by General Partner and Advisors**

Representatives of the General Partner and the Sponsor, including Marcus J. Harrowgate (Managing Partner), Diana R. Castellano (Partner, Co-Head of Investments), Jonathan P. Birch (Partner), and Catherine E. Loomis (General Counsel & Chief Compliance Officer), may attend all meetings of the LPAC in a non-voting capacity and shall be available to respond to questions and present information to the Members.

The General Partner may invite Fund counsel (Calderwood & Harkness LLP), the Fund auditor (Caldwell, Fitch & Hartley LLP), the fund administrator (Pinnacle Fund Services LLC), or other advisors to attend meetings or portions thereof as reasonably necessary in connection with matters on the agenda. The General Partner shall inform the Members in advance of the identities of any non-Member attendees expected at a meeting.

The LPAC may request that certain portions of a meeting be held without representatives of the General Partner present (an \"Executive Session\"). In such event, the General Partner and its representatives shall withdraw from the meeting for the duration of the Executive Session. The Members present during the Executive Session may request that notes of any matters discussed or actions taken during the Executive Session be included (or excluded, as applicable) in the formal minutes. The General Partner shall cooperate in good faith with any reasonable request for an Executive Session.

**[ARTICLE IV --- SCOPE OF AUTHORITY AND RESPONSIBILITIES]{.underline}**

**Section 4.1 --- Conflict of Interest Approvals**

The LPAC shall review and, where required by the Partnership Agreement, approve or consent to transactions involving actual or potential conflicts of interest between the General Partner (or its affiliates, principals, or related persons) and the Fund or the Limited Partners. Such conflicts of interest transactions include, but are not limited to, the following:

> \(a\) **Co-Investment by the General Partner or Affiliates.** Co-investment transactions in which the General Partner, the Sponsor, any principal thereof, or any affiliate invests alongside the Fund on exposure, that involve conflicts of interest or are otherwise within the LPAC\'s scope of authority and advisory responsibility under Article IV of this Charter, shall be reported to the LPAC. The LPAC shall have the same consultative and approval rights with respect to such matters as it has with respect to the Main Fund, to the extent applicable.

**[ARTICLE VI --- COMPENSATION AND EXPENSES]{.underline}**

**Section 6.1 --- No Compensation**

LPAC Members shall receive no compensation from the Fund, the General Partner, the Sponsor, or any affiliate thereof for their service on the LPAC. Membership on the LPAC is undertaken on a voluntary basis as part of the Fund\'s governance framework.

**Section 6.2 --- Reimbursement of Expenses**

Reasonable out-of-pocket expenses incurred by LPAC Members in connection with attendance at LPAC meetings, including travel, lodging, and meals, shall be reimbursable by the Fund as a Fund expense, to the extent approved by the General Partner. Members seeking reimbursement shall submit documentation of such expenses to the General Partner in accordance with the Fund\'s expense reimbursement policies.

Any engagement of independent advisors by the LPAC, including independent valuation firms, legal counsel, or other professionals, shall require the prior written consent of the General Partner (which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed), and the costs thereof shall be borne by the Fund as a Fund expense. The General Partner shall cooperate with the LPAC in the selection and engagement of any such independent advisors.

**[ARTICLE VII --- CONFIDENTIALITY]{.underline}**

**Section 7.1 --- Confidentiality Obligations**

Each Member (and each observer) shall maintain the confidentiality of all non-public information received in connection with its service on the LPAC (\"Confidential Information\"), including, but not limited to:

> \(a\) portfolio company financial information, operating data, and business plans;
>
> \(b\) valuation data, methodologies, models, and conclusions;
>
> \(c\) co-investment opportunities, deal pipeline information, and term sheets;
>
> \(d\) conflict-of-interest disclosures and the substance of any LPAC deliberations related thereto;
>
> \(e\) Fund financial statements, performance data, IRRs, multiples, and capital account information;
>
> \(f\) information relating to the identity, capital commitments, or investment terms of other Limited Partners; and
>
> \(g\) any other proprietary, trade secret, or confidential information of the Fund, the General Partner, the Sponsor, or any portfolio company.

Each Member shall use Confidential Information solely for purposes of fulfilling its responsibilities as a Member of the LPAC and shall not disclose Confidential Information to any third party except as permitted under Section 7.2. Each Member shall take reasonable precautions to protect the confidentiality of Confidential Information, using at least the same degree of care that such Member uses to protect its own confidential information of similar importance.

**Section 7.2 --- Exceptions**

The confidentiality obligations set forth in Section 7.1 shall not apply to information:

> \(a\) that is or becomes publicly available other than through a breach of this Charter or any other confidentiality obligation owed to the Fund or the General Partner;
>
> \(b\) that was known to the Member prior to its receipt from the Fund or the General Partner, as demonstrated by the Member\'s written records, without breach of any other confidentiality obligation;
>
> \(c\) that is independently developed by the Member without use of or reference to Confidential Information;
>
> \(d\) that is required to be disclosed by applicable law, regulation, or legal process, or by a governmental or regulatory authority having jurisdiction over the Member, including, without limitation, disclosures required under state or federal public records laws, freedom of information acts, or similar statutes applicable to governmental plan investors (such as Northmoor State Pension System) or sovereign investors (such as Tidewater Sovereign Investment Authority), *provided* that the Member shall, to the extent legally permissible, provide the General Partner with prompt prior written notice of such required disclosure so that the General Partner may seek an appropriate protective order or other remedy;
>
> \(e\) that is disclosed to the Member\'s professional advisors, auditors, internal and external legal counsel, consultants, or other agents on a need-to-know basis and subject to confidentiality obligations no less restrictive than those set forth herein; or
>
> \(f\) that is disclosed pursuant to the terms of a Side Letter entered into between the General Partner and the applicable Member or the applicable Member\'s governing body or oversight agency.

**Section 7.3 --- Duration**

The confidentiality obligations set forth in this Article VII shall survive the termination and winding up of the Fund for a period of two (2) years following the date of final liquidating distributions to the Limited Partners.

**[ARTICLE VIII --- LIABILITY AND INDEMNIFICATION]{.underline}**

**Section 8.1 --- No Fiduciary Duty**

LPAC Members do not owe fiduciary duties to the Fund, the General Partner, or any Limited Partner by reason of their service on the LPAC. LPAC Members act solely in their capacity as representatives of their respective Limited Partners, and their service on the LPAC shall not create or be deemed to create a relationship of principal and agent, trustee and beneficiary, or any other fiduciary relationship between such Members and the Fund, the General Partner, any other Limited Partner, or any portfolio company. This Section 8.1 is consistent with and supplements the elimination and modification of fiduciary duties set forth in the Partnership Agreement to the fullest extent permitted by the Delaware Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act.

**Section 8.2 --- Limitation of Liability**

No Member shall be liable to the Fund, the General Partner, any Limited Partner, or any other person for any act or omission taken or suffered in good faith in connection with its service on the LPAC, including any approval, consent, waiver, recommendation, vote, or abstention given, withheld, or made, except in the case of such Member\'s fraud, willful misconduct, or bad faith. No Member shall be liable for any action or inaction of the General Partner, for the investment decisions of the Fund, or for the performance of any portfolio investment, whether or not such action, inaction, or decision was the subject of LPAC review or approval.

The foregoing limitation of liability shall apply to the fullest extent permitted by applicable Delaware law and shall be in addition to (and not in limitation of) any limitation of liability afforded to the Member in its capacity as a Limited Partner under the Partnership Agreement or applicable law.

**Section 8.3 --- Indemnification**

The Fund shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless each Member and its Designated Representatives and Alternate Representatives (collectively, \"Indemnified LPAC Persons\") against any and all losses, claims, damages, liabilities, judgments, fines, penalties, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys\' fees and expenses of investigation) arising out of or relating to such Indemnified LPAC Person\'s service on the LPAC, to the fullest extent permitted by the Partnership Agreement and applicable Delaware law, except to the extent that such losses, claims, damages, liabilities, or expenses result from the Indemnified LPAC Person\'s fraud, willful misconduct, or bad faith.

Indemnification obligations under this Section 8.3 are obligations of the Fund (and, accordingly, are borne indirectly by the Limited Partners as Fund expenses) and not of the General Partner individually, except as may otherwise be provided in the Partnership Agreement. The procedures for asserting and processing indemnification claims shall be as set forth in the Partnership Agreement.

**Section 8.4 --- Insurance**

The General Partner may, in its discretion, cause the Fund to obtain directors\' and officers\' liability insurance or similar liability insurance covering LPAC Members and their Designated Representatives and Alternate Representatives in connection with their service on the LPAC, the cost of which shall be borne as a Fund expense. The General Partner shall inform the LPAC of the existence, scope, and material terms of any such insurance policy upon request.

**[ARTICLE IX --- AMENDMENTS]{.underline}**

**Section 9.1 --- Amendment Procedure**

This Charter may be amended, modified, or supplemented by the General Partner with the prior approval of a majority of the LPAC Members then serving. All amendments shall be in writing and shall be effective upon execution by the General Partner and delivery of written notice to all Members (and observers, if applicable). No amendment to this Charter shall diminish the rights of any Member under this Charter without such Member\'s prior written consent, unless such diminution applies equally to all Members.

For the avoidance of doubt, amendments to the Partnership Agreement that affect the authority, composition, or responsibilities of the LPAC shall be governed by the amendment provisions of the Partnership Agreement, and any resulting changes to this Charter shall be adopted in accordance with this Section 9.1.

**[ARTICLE X --- GENERAL PROVISIONS]{.underline}**

**Section 10.1 --- Governing Law**

This Charter shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to its conflicts of law principles that would result in the application of the laws of any other jurisdiction.

**Section 10.2 --- Dispute Resolution**

Any dispute, controversy, or claim arising under, out of, or in connection with this Charter, including any question regarding its existence, validity, interpretation, performance, breach, or termination, shall be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the Court of Chancery of the State of Delaware (or, if the Court of Chancery of the State of Delaware lacks subject matter jurisdiction, the Superior Court of the State of Delaware, New Castle County), consistent with the dispute resolution provisions of the Partnership Agreement. Each Member, by accepting appointment to the LPAC, consents to the personal jurisdiction of such courts and waives any objection to venue therein.

**Section 10.3 --- Relationship to Partnership Agreement**

This Charter is supplemental to and subject to the Partnership Agreement in all respects. In the event of any conflict or inconsistency between the provisions of this Charter and the provisions of the Partnership Agreement, the Partnership Agreement shall control and govern. References herein to sections of the Partnership Agreement are to the corresponding sections of the Agreement of Limited Partnership of Harrowgate Private Equity Fund V LP, as amended, restated, supplemented, or otherwise modified from time to time.

**Section 10.4 --- Notices**

All notices, requests, demands, consents, and other communications under this Charter shall be delivered in writing to the addresses (including email addresses) set forth in each Member\'s Subscription Agreement or as subsequently updated in writing by the applicable Member to the General Partner. Notices shall be deemed delivered upon receipt (or, in the case of email, upon transmission without receipt of an automated delivery failure notification).

Notices to the General Partner shall be delivered to:

> Harrowgate Fund V GP LLC c/o Harrowgate Capital Partners LLC 1200 Concord Pike, Suite 600 Wilmington, Delaware 19803
>
> Attention: Catherine E. Loomis, General Counsel & Chief Compliance Officer
>
> Email: c.loomis@harrowgatecapital.com
>
> With a copy (which shall not constitute notice) to:
>

>
> Email: r.overton@harrowgatecapital.com

**Section 10.5 --- Severability**

If any provision of this Charter is held by a court of competent jurisdiction to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable for any reason, such invalidity, illegality, or unenforceability shall not affect any other provision of this Charter, and this Charter shall be construed as if such invalid, illegal, or unenforceable provision had never been contained herein. In such event, the remaining provisions of this Charter shall continue in full force and effect, and the parties shall negotiate in good faith to replace the invalid, illegal, or unenforceable provision with a valid and enforceable provision that most closely approximates the original intent of the parties.

**Section 10.6 --- Entire Understanding**

This Charter, together with the Partnership Agreement and any applicable Side Letters, constitutes the entire understanding among the General Partner and the LPAC Members with respect to the establishment, composition, authority, and operation of the LPAC. This Charter supersedes all prior discussions, negotiations, and agreements, whether written or oral, relating to the subject matter hereof.

107: Each of these anchor investors will execute a separate side letter agreement that supplements the Amended and Restated Limited Partnership Agreement of Pinnacle Venture Fund II LP (the "LPA"), which is expected to be dated as of the First Close on January 15, 2026. The side letters will grant various economic, governance, informational, and operational accommodations tailored to the legal status, investment policy requirements, and negotiating priorities of each anchor LP.
108: The key timeline milestones are as follows: initial drafts of the three anchor side letters are targeted for distribution to counterparty counsel by October 20, 2025; the negotiation period is expected to extend through December 20, 2025 (with two to three rounds of mark-ups anticipated per side letter); the First Close is targeted for January 15, 2026; and the Final Close deadline is July 15, 2026. The MFN Side Letter Compilation will be delivered to all MFN-eligible limited partners within fifteen (15) business days following the Final Close.
109: Our central recommendation is to structure the MFN framework with robust "Excluded Provisions" carve-outs designed to limit the GP's economic and operational exposure from subsequent LP elections, while providing sufficient MFN coverage to satisfy the institutional expectations of sophisticated anchor investors. Specifically, we recommend defining five categories of Excluded Provisions (governmental plan regulatory requirements, ERISA representations, advisory committee seats, portfolio company board observer rights, and a catch-all for LP-specific legal/regulatory/tax provisions) while permitting MFN elections for economic terms (management fee reductions, co-investment terms, fee netting) and information/notification rights.
110: The principal economic terms of the Fund, as set forth in the LPA, are summarized below:
111: Target Fund Size and Hard Cap. The Fund's target aggregate capital commitments are $600,000,000. The LPA provides for a hard cap of $750,000,000, above which no additional commitments may be accepted without the consent of a majority-in-interest of the existing limited partners. The $150,000,000 buffer between the target and the hard cap provides meaningful flexibility for the GP to accommodate additional investor interest, particularly from institutional investors who may increase their commitments following the First Close.
112: Carried Interest. The GP is entitled to a carried interest of 20% of net profits over an 8% preferred return (compounded annually). The LPA provides for a 100% GP catch-up to a 20/80 split once the preferred return has been fully distributed. Thereafter, all distributions are split 80% to the limited partners and 20% to the GP. The carried interest structure is standard for venture capital funds and is not a point of significant negotiation with the anchor LPs.
113: Fund Term. The Fund has a term of ten (10) years from the First Close, with a scheduled termination date of January 15, 2036. The LPA provides the GP with discretion to extend the term for up to two (2) additional one-year periods (i.e., through January 15, 2037, and if further extended, through January 15, 2038), subject to the GP's good faith determination that such extensions are necessary or desirable to facilitate the orderly liquidation of remaining portfolio investments.
114: Fund Administrator: Meridian Fund Services LLC. The Fund's administrator is Meridian Fund Services LLC, with Patricia Lam serving as the designated Relationship Manager. Meridian will be responsible for NAV calculations, capital call and distribution processing, investor reporting, and investor relations support. Several of the provisions under negotiation in the anchor side letters — including enhanced quarterly reporting with sector-level attribution (CPERS) and ILPA-aligned information rights (Brindoval) — will require coordination with Meridian and may increase the scope (and cost) of the administration engagement. We recommend confirming with Meridian, through Patricia Lam, the operational feasibility and incremental cost implications of enhanced reporting commitments before finalizing the side letter drafts.
115: Fund Auditor: Ashford & Whitmore LLP. The Fund's auditor is Ashford & Whitmore LLP, with Richard Noonan serving as the Engagement Partner. Ashford & Whitmore will perform the annual financial statement audit of the Fund. The auditor engagement is standard and is not directly implicated by the side letter negotiations, although certain side letter provisions (such as ILPA-aligned reporting) may reference audited financial statements and impose timing requirements for delivery of audit reports.
116: The most favored nation clause is a standard feature in institutional fund side letters, particularly for anchor and early-closing investors. The MFN clause provides qualifying limited partners with the right to elect into more favorable terms that may be granted to other investors in the Fund, whether at the same closing or at subsequent closings. The purpose of the MFN clause is to protect early investors from economic disadvantage relative to later investors who may negotiate more favorable terms, and to provide a mechanism for equalizing the treatment of similarly situated limited partners.
117: The MFN framework will be implemented as follows: each anchor side letter will include an MFN election right provision, and the same provision (or a substantively identical provision) will be included in the side letters of all subsequent LPs whose commitments meet or exceed the MFN eligibility threshold. Separately, the GP will prepare a template MFN Election Procedures Letter and MFN Election Form, which will be distributed as part of the side letter package following the Final Close. All side letters, the LPA, and the MFN framework documents will be governed by the laws of the State of Delaware.
118: We recommend establishing the MFN eligibility threshold at a commitment amount of $25,000,000 or greater to the Fund. Only limited partners whose aggregate capital commitments (including any commitments made at subsequent closings) equal or exceed $25,000,000 will be entitled to exercise MFN election rights.
119: •  GP expectations regarding LP base. The GP has indicated that it expects the Fund's LP base to consist of approximately twenty to twenty-five limited partners, with the majority committing $25,000,000 or more. The $25M threshold thus captures the core institutional LP base while excluding a small number of smaller investors who may be admitted at later closings.
120: Preservation of LP confidentiality. There is no requirement for the GP to notify the limited partner whose term was elected into by another LP. The confidentiality of each LP's identity and the specific terms of its side letter are preserved throughout the MFN process. The MFN Side Letter Compilation itself is delivered on a confidential basis and is subject to the confidentiality provisions of the LPA.
121: The first category of Excluded Provisions covers any provision that is included in a side letter to satisfy the specific legal or regulatory requirements of a limited partner that is a governmental pension plan, governmental retirement system, or sovereign entity. This category is designed to capture provisions that are legally mandated for governmental investors and that have no economic value, relevance, or applicability to non-governmental limited partners.
122: The second category of Excluded Provisions covers representations that a limited partner is not subject to the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974, as amended ("ERISA"), or waivers of ERISA-related representations that may be included in the LPA.
123: The primary beneficiary of this exclusion is Northstar Endowment Partners LLC, which is an investment vehicle for the endowment of Veltrano University. As a university endowment, NEP is not an "employee benefit plan" within the meaning of ERISA Section 3(3), and is not subject to the fiduciary duty, prohibited transaction, or plan asset rules of ERISA. NEP's side letter will include a representation that it is not a "benefit plan investor" (as defined in 29 C.F.R. § 2510.3-101) and a waiver of any ERISA-related representations that may be included in the LPA.
124: The third category of Excluded Provisions covers the right to designate a representative to the Fund's advisory committee (also referred to as the LP Advisory Committee or "LPAC").
125: The primary beneficiary of this exclusion is Northstar Endowment Partners LLC, which has been granted a seat on the Fund's advisory committee through its side letter. We note, however, that CPERS is separately entitled to an advisory committee seat under the LPA itself, as a limited partner with a commitment of $50,000,000 or more. CPERS's advisory committee entitlement does not arise from the side letter and therefore does not create MFN exposure; however, this distinction should be noted clearly in the CPERS side letter to avoid any ambiguity.
126: This is a forward-looking exclusion designed to protect the GP's flexibility, and we do not anticipate that it will be a point of negotiation with the anchor LPs or their counsel.
127: •  ILPA-aligned information rights
128: Sandra Okafor of Whitfield & Gage LLP is experienced public pension fund counsel who has represented CPERS and other Pacific Northwest governmental plans in numerous fund investment transactions. We should anticipate detailed and informed comments on FOIA protections, excuse rights, fiduciary duty provisions, and the scope of Excluded Provisions in the MFN framework. Ms. Okafor is likely to push for a narrow definition of Excluded Provisions to maximize CPERS's own MFN election power (i.e., to ensure that CPERS can elect into favorable terms granted to subsequent LPs). This creates a strategic tension: CPERS benefits from a broad MFN-eligible category (which expands the universe of terms it can elect into) but also benefits from the exclusion of its own governmental plan provisions (which prevents non-governmental LPs from electing into terms designed for CPERS).
129: Recommendation: We recommend confirming with Meridian (through Patricia Lam) that sector-level attribution is operationally feasible within the current administration engagement scope and budget. If enhanced reporting will increase administration costs, we recommend adding a provision in the side letter (and in the LPA, if necessary) that permits fund-level operational costs attributable to enhanced reporting to be charged as a Fund expense.
130: •  A requirement that CPERS provide written notice to the GP within a specified period (recommend five (5) business days) before disclosing any Fund information in response to a public records request;
131: We note that CPERS is separately entitled to an advisory committee seat under the LPA itself, as a limited partner whose capital commitment equals or exceeds $50,000,000. CPERS's advisory committee entitlement does not arise from its side letter and therefore does not create MFN exposure. However, this distinction should be noted clearly in the CPERS side letter to avoid any suggestion that the advisory committee seat is a side letter provision subject to MFN.
132: NEP has requested a provision requiring the GP to provide written notice to NEP within a specified period following the occurrence of a "key-person event." The key persons designated in the LPA are Rajesh Mehta and Claire Dubois, both of whom are required to devote substantially all of their business time and attention to the affairs of the Fund during the investment period.
133: A "key-person event" would include the death, disability, departure, or failure of either key person to devote substantially all of his or her business time to the Fund. The LPA already addresses the consequences of a key-person event (including a potential suspension of the investment period), but the side letter provision would impose an affirmative notification obligation on the GP, requiring written notice to NEP within a specified number of business days of the event.
134: NEP's side letter will include a representation that NEP is not a "benefit plan investor" within the meaning of 29 C.F.R. § 2510.3-101 and a waiver of any ERISA-related representations or covenants that may be included in the LPA. This representation is factually accurate (NEP is a university endowment vehicle, not an employee benefit plan) and serves to confirm that the Fund's assets will not be treated as "plan assets" subject to ERISA by virtue of NEP's investment.
135: (d) Information Rights Aligned with ILPA Best Practices.  Classification: MFN-Eligible.
136: Brindoval has requested information rights aligned with the best practices published by the Institutional Limited Partners Association ("ILPA"). ILPA best practices encompass a broad range of reporting and disclosure standards, including:
137: •  Standardized reporting templates designed to facilitate comparability across fund investments.
138: We recommend classifying this provision as MFN-eligible. ILPA-aligned reporting is an information right of general applicability that is not specific to any particular LP's legal or regulatory status. Most institutional LPs now expect ILPA-aligned reporting as a baseline, and providing these rights through the side letter (rather than the LPA) is a common market practice that allows the GP to tailor the scope and timing of enhanced reporting to institutional investors while maintaining more limited reporting for smaller investors.
139: The operational impact of ILPA-aligned reporting should be coordinated with Meridian Fund Services LLC (Patricia Lam) to ensure that the fund administration engagement is scoped and budgeted appropriately. If enhanced reporting will increase administration costs, those costs should be treated as fund expenses.
140: Recommendation: MFN-eligible. Generally low risk, as most institutional LPs expect ILPA-aligned reporting regardless of whether it is formally included in the side letter. No significant mitigation measures recommended.
141: •  Enhanced reporting: MFN elections into enhanced reporting provisions (sector-level attribution, ILPA-aligned reporting) increase operational costs by requiring additional data analysis and report preparation from Meridian Fund Services LLC. While these costs may be charged as fund expenses, they nonetheless reduce net returns to all LPs (including the GP, to the extent of its Fund commitment).
142: 1.  Robust Excluded Provisions definition. The five categories of Excluded Provisions described in Section IV are designed to capture LP-specific regulatory, legal, and governance accommodations that should not be subject to MFN election. The breadth and specificity of these categories are the GP's primary structural protection against unlimited MFN exposure.
143: 3.  Sunset provision. Consider including a "sunset" mechanism providing that MFN elections apply only to side letter terms granted before the Final Close, and do not extend to amendments, supplements, or side letters entered into after the MFN Election Period. This prevents the GP from being locked into an MFN framework indefinitely and preserves flexibility for post-closing accommodations.
144: ILPA-aligned information rights
145: •  Uniform LPA cross-references. All side letters should contain a uniform cross-reference to the governing agreement: "This Side Letter supplements the Amended and Restated Limited Partnership Agreement of Pinnacle Venture Fund II LP, dated as of January 15, 2026 (as may be further amended, restated, supplemented, or otherwise modified from time to time, the 'LPA')." Any amendments to the LPA after the First Close should be reflected in a corresponding update to the side letter cross-reference.
146: •  Governing law. All side letters are governed by the laws of the State of Delaware, consistent with the LPA. The governing law clause should be identical across all three side letters.

All side letters and the LPA are governed by the laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to conflict of law principles that would result in the application of the laws of any other jurisdiction.

Instructions for Use. Each item in this Checklist should be marked with its current status (using the Status Legend set forth on the cover page) and the date on which the status was last updated. (a) Management Fee Reduction. Reduction of the management fee payable by CPERS to 1.75% per annum on committed capital during the Investment Period (representing a 25 basis point discount from the standard 2.00% management fee set forth in Section 6.1 of the LPA). All inquiries and document deliveries related to the items on this Checklist should be directed to the appropriate contact identified below. 1.  Scope of This Checklist. This Checklist covers only the side letter package deliverables for the three anchor limited partners participating at the First Close of Pinnacle Venture Fund II LP. The main Fund Closing Checklist (prepared and maintained separately by C&H) covers all other First Close deliverables, including but not limited to: (a) subscription agreements for all limited partners admitted at the First Close; (b) execution of the LPA by all limited partners and the General Partner; (c) partnership tax matters, including collection of IRS Forms W-9 or W-8 (as applicable), FATCA/CRS classifications, and tax identification numbers; (d) state and federal regulatory filings (including state "blue sky" filings, if required); (e) banking and custody arrangements for the Fund's accounts; (f) insurance certificates (including directors and officers liability insurance for the General Partner); and (g) other organizational and administrative matters.

Any disputes arising under the side letters or the LPA are subject to the dispute resolution provisions set forth in the LPA (including, if applicable, mandatory arbitration before the American Arbitration Association in accordance with its Commercial Arbitration Rules).

===== documents/matters/1002-00003/Memos & Analyses/side-letter-strategy-and-mfn-framework-memo.docx =====

PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT This memorandum is protected by the attorney-client privilege and the work product doctrine. It is intended solely for the use of the attorneys and personnel of Calderwood & Harkness LLP and should not be disclosed to any third party without the prior written consent of the undersigned.

Each of these anchor investors will execute a separate side letter agreement that supplements the Amended and Restated Limited Partnership Agreement of Pinnacle Venture Fund II LP (the "LPA"), which is expected to be dated as of the First Close on January 15, 2026. The side letters will grant various economic, governance, informational, and operational accommodations tailored to the legal status, investment policy requirements, and negotiating priorities of each anchor LP.

The key timeline milestones are as follows: initial drafts of the three anchor side letters are targeted for distribution to counterparty counsel by October 20, 2025; the negotiation period is expected to extend through December 20, 2025 (with two to three rounds of mark-ups anticipated per side letter); the First Close is targeted for January 15, 2026; and the Final Close deadline is July 15, 2026. The MFN Side Letter Compilation will be delivered to all MFN-eligible limited partners within fifteen (15) business days following the Final Close.

Our central recommendation is to structure the MFN framework with robust "Excluded Provisions" carve-outs designed to limit the GP's economic and operational exposure from subsequent LP elections, while providing sufficient MFN coverage to satisfy the institutional expectations of sophisticated anchor investors. Specifically, we recommend defining five categories of Excluded Provisions (governmental plan regulatory requirements, ERISA representations, advisory committee seats, portfolio company board observer rights, and a catch-all for LP-specific legal/regulatory/tax provisions) while permitting MFN elections for economic terms (management fee reductions, co-investment terms, fee netting) and information/notification rights.
The principal economic terms of the Fund, as set forth in the LPA, are summarized below:

Target Fund Size and Hard Cap. The Fund's target aggregate capital commitments are $600,000,000. The LPA provides for a hard cap of $750,000,000, above which no additional commitments may be accepted without the consent of a majority-in-interest of the existing limited partners. The $150,000,000 buffer between the target and the hard cap provides meaningful flexibility for the GP to accommodate additional investor interest, particularly from institutional investors who may increase their commitments following the First Close.

Carried Interest. The GP is entitled to a carried interest of 20% of net profits over an 8% preferred return (compounded annually). The LPA provides for a 100% GP catch-up to a 20/80 split once the preferred return has been fully distributed. Thereafter, all distributions are split 80% to the limited partners and 20% to the GP. The carried interest structure is standard for venture capital funds and is not a point of significant negotiation with the anchor LPs.

Fund Term. The Fund has a term of ten (10) years from the First Close, with a scheduled termination date of January 15, 2036. The LPA provides the GP with discretion to extend the term for up to two (2) additional one-year periods (i.e., through January 15, 2037, and if further extended, through January 15, 2038), subject to the GP's good faith determination that such extensions are necessary or desirable to facilitate the orderly liquidation of remaining portfolio investments.

Fund Administrator: Meridian Fund Services LLC. The Fund's administrator is Meridian Fund Services LLC, with Patricia Lam serving as the designated Relationship Manager. Meridian will be responsible for NAV calculations, capital call and distribution processing, investor reporting, and investor relations support. Several of the provisions under negotiation in the anchor side letters — including enhanced quarterly reporting with sector-level attribution (CPERS) and ILPA-aligned information rights (Brindoval) — will require coordination with Meridian and may increase the scope (and cost) of the administration engagement. We recommend confirming with Meridian, through Patricia Lam, the operational feasibility and incremental cost implications of enhanced reporting commitments before finalizing the side letter drafts.

Fund Auditor: Ashford & Whitmore LLP. The Fund's auditor is Ashford & Whitmore LLP, with Richard Noonan serving as the Engagement Partner. Ashford & Whitmore will perform the annual financial statement audit of the Fund. The auditor engagement is standard and is not directly implicated by the side letter negotiations, although certain side letter provisions (such as ILPA-aligned reporting) may reference audited financial statements and impose timing requirements for delivery of audit reports.

The most favored nation clause is a standard feature in institutional fund side letters, particularly for anchor and early-closing investors. The MFN clause provides qualifying limited partners with the right to elect into more favorable terms that may be granted to other investors in the Fund, whether at the same closing or at subsequent closings. The purpose of the MFN clause is to protect early investors from economic disadvantage relative to later investors who may negotiate more favorable terms, and to provide a mechanism for equalizing the treatment of similarly situated limited partners.

The MFN framework will be implemented as follows: each anchor side letter will include an MFN election right provision, and the same provision (or a substantively identical provision) will be included in the side letters of all subsequent LPs whose commitments meet or exceed the MFN eligibility threshold. Separately, the GP will prepare a template MFN Election Procedures Letter and MFN Election Form, which will be distributed as part of the side letter package following the Final Close. All side letters, the LPA, and the MFN framework documents will be governed by the laws of the State of Delaware.

We recommend establishing the MFN eligibility threshold at a commitment amount of $25,000,000 or greater to the Fund. Only limited partners whose aggregate capital commitments (including any commitments made at subsequent closings) equal or exceed $25,000,000 will be entitled to exercise MFN election rights.

•  GP expectations regarding LP base. The GP has indicated that it expects the Fund's LP base to consist of approximately twenty to twenty-five limited partners, with the majority committing $25,000,000 or more. The $25M threshold thus captures the core institutional LP base while excluding a small number of smaller investors who may be admitted at later closings.

Preservation of LP confidentiality. There is no requirement for the GP to notify the limited partner whose term was elected into by another LP. The confidentiality of each LP's identity and the specific terms of its side letter are preserved throughout the MFN process. The MFN Side Letter Compilation itself is delivered on a confidential basis and is subject to the confidentiality provisions of the LPA.

The first category of Excluded Provisions covers any provision that is included in a side letter to satisfy the specific legal or regulatory requirements of a limited partner that is a governmental pension plan, governmental retirement system, or sovereign entity. This category is designed to capture provisions that are legally mandated for governmental investors and that have no economic value, relevance, or applicability to non-governmental limited partners.

The second category of Excluded Provisions covers representations that a limited partner is not subject to the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974, as amended ("ERISA"), or waivers of ERISA-related representations that may be included in the LPA.

The primary beneficiary of this exclusion is Northstar Endowment Partners LLC, which is an investment vehicle for the endowment of Veltrano University. As a university endowment, NEP is not an "employee benefit plan" within the meaning of ERISA Section 3(3), and is not subject to the fiduciary duty, prohibited transaction, or plan asset rules of ERISA. NEP's side letter will include a representation that it is not a "benefit plan investor" (as defined in 29 C.F.R. § 2510.3-101) and a waiver of any ERISA-related representations that may be included in the LPA.
The third category of Excluded Provisions covers the right to designate a representative to the Fund's advisory committee (also referred to as the LP Advisory Committee or "LPAC").

The primary beneficiary of this exclusion is Northstar Endowment Partners LLC, which has been granted a seat on the Fund's advisory committee through its side letter. We note, however, that CPERS is separately entitled to an advisory committee seat under the LPA itself, as a limited partner with a commitment of $50,000,000 or more. CPERS's advisory committee entitlement does not arise from the side letter and therefore does not create MFN exposure; however, this distinction should be noted clearly in the CPERS side letter to avoid any ambiguity.
This is a forward-looking exclusion designed to protect the GP's flexibility, and we do not anticipate that it will be a point of negotiation with the anchor LPs or their counsel.
•  ILPA-aligned information rights

Sandra Okafor of Whitfield & Gage LLP is experienced public pension fund counsel who has represented CPERS and other Pacific Northwest governmental plans in numerous fund investment transactions. We should anticipate detailed and informed comments on FOIA protections, excuse rights, fiduciary duty provisions, and the scope of Excluded Provisions in the MFN framework. Ms. Okafor is likely to push for a narrow definition of Excluded Provisions to maximize CPERS's own MFN election power (i.e., to ensure that CPERS can elect into favorable terms granted to subsequent LPs). This creates a strategic tension: CPERS benefits from a broad MFN-eligible category (which expands the universe of terms it can elect into) but also benefits from the exclusion of its own governmental plan provisions (which prevents non-governmental LPs from electing into terms designed for CPERS).

Recommendation: We recommend confirming with Meridian (through Patricia Lam) that sector-level attribution is operationally feasible within the current administration engagement scope and budget. If enhanced reporting will increase administration costs, we recommend adding a provision in the side letter (and in the LPA, if necessary) that permits fund-level operational costs attributable to enhanced reporting to be charged as a Fund expense.

•  A requirement that CPERS provide written notice to the GP within a specified period (recommend five (5) business days) before disclosing any Fund information in response to a public records request;

We note that CPERS is separately entitled to an advisory committee seat under the LPA itself, as a limited partner whose capital commitment equals or exceeds $50,000,000. CPERS's advisory committee entitlement does not arise from its side letter and therefore does not create MFN exposure. However, this distinction should be noted clearly in the CPERS side letter to avoid any suggestion that the advisory committee seat is a side letter provision subject to MFN.

NEP has requested a provision requiring the GP to provide written notice to NEP within a specified period following the occurrence of a "key-person event." The key persons designated in the LPA are Rajesh Mehta and Claire Dubois, both of whom are required to devote substantially all of their business time and attention to the affairs of the Fund during the investment period.

A "key-person event" would include the death, disability, departure, or failure of either key person to devote substantially all of his or her business time to the Fund. The LPA already addresses the consequences of a key-person event (including a potential suspension of the investment period), but the side letter provision would impose an affirmative notification obligation on the GP, requiring written notice to NEP within a specified number of business days of the event.

NEP's side letter will include a representation that NEP is not a "benefit plan investor" within the meaning of 29 C.F.R. § 2510.3-101 and a waiver of any ERISA-related representations or covenants that may be included in the LPA. This representation is factually accurate (NEP is a university endowment vehicle, not an employee benefit plan) and serves to confirm that the Fund's assets will not be treated as "plan assets" subject to ERISA by virtue of NEP's investment.
(d) Information Rights Aligned with ILPA Best Practices.  Classification: MFN-Eligible.

Brindoval has requested information rights aligned with the best practices published by the Institutional Limited Partners Association ("ILPA"). ILPA best practices encompass a broad range of reporting and disclosure standards, including:
•  Standardized reporting templates designed to facilitate comparability across fund investments.

We recommend classifying this provision as MFN-eligible. ILPA-aligned reporting is an information right of general applicability that is not specific to any particular LP's legal or regulatory status. Most institutional LPs now expect ILPA-aligned reporting as a baseline, and providing these rights through the side letter (rather than the LPA) is a common market practice that allows the GP to tailor the scope and timing of enhanced reporting to institutional investors while maintaining more limited reporting for smaller investors.

The operational impact of ILPA-aligned reporting should be coordinated with Meridian Fund Services LLC (Patricia Lam) to ensure that the fund administration engagement is scoped and budgeted appropriately. If enhanced reporting will increase administration costs, those costs should be treated as fund expenses.

Recommendation: MFN-eligible. Generally low risk, as most institutional LPs expect ILPA-aligned reporting regardless of whether it is formally included in the side letter. No significant mitigation measures recommended.

•  Enhanced reporting: MFN elections into enhanced reporting provisions (sector-level attribution, ILPA-aligned reporting) increase operational costs by requiring additional data analysis and report preparation from Meridian Fund Services LLC. While these costs may be charged as fund expenses, they nonetheless reduce net returns to all LPs (including the GP, to the extent of its Fund commitment).

1.  Robust Excluded Provisions definition. The five categories of Excluded Provisions described in Section IV are designed to capture LP-specific regulatory, legal, and governance accommodations that should not be subject to MFN election. The breadth and specificity of these categories are the GP's primary structural protection against unlimited MFN exposure.

3.  Sunset provision. Consider including a "sunset" mechanism providing that MFN elections apply only to side letter terms granted before the Final Close, and do not extend to amendments, supplements, or side letters entered into after the MFN Election Period. This prevents the GP from being locked into an MFN framework indefinitely and preserves flexibility for post-closing accommodations.
ILPA-aligned information rights

•  Uniform LPA cross-references. All side letters should contain a uniform cross-reference to the governing agreement: "This Side Letter supplements the Amended and Restated Limited Partnership Agreement of Pinnacle Venture Fund II LP, dated as of January 15, 2026 (as may be further amended, restated, supplemented, or otherwise modified from time to time, the 'LPA')." Any amendments to the LPA after the First Close should be reflected in a corresponding update to the side letter cross-reference.
•  Governing law. All side letters are governed by the laws of the State of Delaware, consistent with the LPA. The governing law clause should be identical across all three side letters.

Re: Engagement of Calderwood & Harkness LLP — Private Letter Ruling Request in Connection with Cross-Border Fund-Platform Reorganization of Solara Digital Infrastructure LP
Engagement Number: 20250527-SDILP-PLR
Calderwood & Harkness LLP ("Calderwood & Harkness" or the "Firm") is pleased to confirm its engagement by Solara Digital Infrastructure LP ("Solara" or "SDILP"), a Delaware limited partnership, and its general partner, Solara Digital Infrastructure GP LLC ("Solara GP"), a Delaware limited liability company (collectively, the "Client"), to provide the legal services described in this engagement letter (this "Letter"). We appreciate the confidence that Solara and Solara GP have placed in our Firm, and we look forward to working with your team on this significant and complex matter.
This Letter sets forth the terms and conditions upon which Calderwood & Harkness will provide legal services in connection with the matter described herein. By countersigning this Letter in the space provided below, the Client agrees to be bound by the terms and conditions set forth herein. This engagement shall be effective as of the date of the countersignature below. No attorney-client relationship will be deemed to have been established with respect to the matter described herein until this Letter has been signed by an authorized representative of the Client and returned to the Firm.
2. Description of the Client
The client for this engagement is Solara Digital Infrastructure LP (EIN: 82-4917366) and Solara Digital Infrastructure GP LLC (EIN: 82-4917365). ("Pinnacle" or "PHS"), a Delaware corporation headquartered in Charlotte, North Carolina. Pinnacle is a specialty healthcare services platform that owns and operates a network of ambulatory surgical centers ("ASCs") and physician practice management entities across nine states. Pinnacle's operations span a broad geographic footprint, with significant concentrations in the southeastern United States, and the company has established itself as a meaningful participant in the delivery of outpatient surgical and practice management services.
3: Relevant Product Markets. The Firm will analyze the relevant product markets implicated by the proposed transaction. Based on our preliminary understanding of Pinnacle's operations, the primary relevant product markets are expected to include (i) ambulatory surgical center services, encompassing outpatient surgical procedures performed in freestanding ASC facilities, and (ii) physician practice management services, encompassing the management, administrative support, and operational services provided to physician practices under management services agreements or similar arrangements. The Firm will evaluate the appropriate product market definitions in light of applicable case law, FTC and DOJ enforcement actions in the healthcare sector, and the 2023 Merger Guidelines.
4: Relevant Geographic Markets. The Firm will conduct a Metropolitan Statistical Area ("MSA")-level geographic market analysis across Pinnacle's nine-state operational footprint, which includes facilities and operations in North Carolina, South Carolina, Virginia, Tennessee, Georgia, Florida, Alabama, Ohio, and Texas. The geographic market analysis will assess the competitive conditions in each MSA in which Pinnacle operates one or more ASCs or manages physician practices, taking into account patient travel patterns, payor contracting dynamics, and referral source characteristics.
5: Horizontal Overlap Analysis. The Firm will analyze potential horizontal competitive overlaps between Pinnacle and Ardent Capital's existing healthcare portfolio companies, specifically: (i) Marlowe Asset Management Rehabilitation Holdings LLC ("Marlowe Asset Management"), which operates outpatient physical therapy clinics in Texas, Florida, and Georgia; and (ii) Clearpath Diagnostics Inc. ("Clearpath"), which provides clinical laboratory services in Pennsylvania, New Jersey, and New York. Although the services provided by Marlowe Asset Management (outpatient physical therapy) and Clearpath (clinical laboratory services) are distinct from the services provided by Pinnacle (ASC services and physician practice management), the Firm will assess whether any theory of horizontal competition could be advanced by the reviewing agency, including with respect to any ancillary service lines or overlapping payor relationships.

We are pleased to confirm that Calderwood & Harkness LLP ("the Firm," "Calderwood & Harkness," "we," or "us") has been engaged by Ardent Capital Partners III LP ("Ardent Capital," "Fund III," or "you"), a Delaware limited partnership, to provide antitrust and competition law advisory services in connection with Ardent Capital's proposed acquisition of one hundred percent (100%) of the outstanding equity interests of Pinnacle Health Systems, Inc. ("Pinnacle" or "PHS"), a Delaware corporation headquartered in Charlotte, North Carolina. Pinnacle is a specialty healthcare services platform that owns and operates a network of ambulatory surgical centers ("ASCs") and physician practice management entities across nine states. Pinnacle's operations span a broad geographic footprint, with significant concentrations in the southeastern United States, and the company has established itself as a meaningful participant in the delivery of outpatient surgical and practice management services.

Relevant Product Markets. The Firm will analyze the relevant product markets implicated by the proposed transaction. Based on our preliminary understanding of Pinnacle's operations, the primary relevant product markets are expected to include (i) ambulatory surgical center services, encompassing outpatient surgical procedures performed in freestanding ASC facilities, and (ii) physician practice management services, encompassing the management, administrative support, and operational services provided to physician practices under management services agreements or similar arrangements. The Firm will evaluate the appropriate product market definitions in light of applicable case law, FTC and DOJ enforcement actions in the healthcare sector, and the 2023 Merger Guidelines.

Relevant Geographic Markets. The Firm will conduct a Metropolitan Statistical Area ("MSA")-level geographic market analysis across Pinnacle's nine-state operational footprint, which includes facilities and operations in North Carolina, South Carolina, Virginia, Tennessee, Georgia, Florida, Alabama, Ohio, and Texas. The geographic market analysis will assess the competitive conditions in each MSA in which Pinnacle operates one or more ASCs or manages physician practices, taking into account patient travel patterns, payor contracting dynamics, and referral source characteristics.

Horizontal Overlap Analysis. The Firm will analyze potential horizontal competitive overlaps between Pinnacle and Ardent Capital's existing healthcare portfolio companies, specifically: (i) Marlowe Asset Management Rehabilitation Holdings LLC ("Marlowe Asset Management"), which operates outpatient physical therapy clinics in Texas, Florida, and Georgia; and (ii) Clearpath Diagnostics Inc. ("Clearpath"), which provides clinical laboratory services in Pennsylvania, New Jersey, and New York. Although the services provided by Marlowe Asset Management (outpatient physical therapy) and Clearpath (clinical laboratory services) are distinct from the services provided by Pinnacle (ASC services and physician practice management), the Firm will assess whether any theory of horizontal competition could be advanced by the reviewing agency, including with respect to any ancillary service lines or overlapping payor relationships.

Mr. Bellamy is a partner in the Firm's Antitrust & Competition Practice Group and has extensive experience advising private equity sponsors, strategic acquirors, and other clients on HSR filings, merger clearance, and antitrust regulatory matters across a wide range of industries, including healthcare services. Mr. Bellamy will personally participate in all material communications with the reviewing agency and will lead any advocacy efforts before the FTC or DOJ.

Ms. Reyes will have day-to-day responsibility for the preparation of the HSR filing, supervision of the Item 4(c) and Item 4(d) document collection and review process, and drafting of the substantive antitrust analysis memoranda and the voluntary submission (white paper) to FTC staff.
