>
> \(ii\) **Scope of IAC-Designated Independent Investment Committee Member\'s Authority.** WCA advocated for enhanced authority for the IAC-designated independent member of the Investment Committee, including a veto right over investments exceeding a specified threshold. C&H, after consultation with DCM, agreed to grant the independent member a consultative role and a negative consent right on any single investment exceeding 5% of the Fund\'s NAV, but resisted the imposition of a general veto right, which C&H advised would be inconsistent with the General Partner\'s fiduciary obligations and the Fund\'s operational requirements.
>
> \(iii\) **Follow-On Investment Cap Reduction.** WCA endorsed the proposed reduction of the follow-on investment cap from 1.0% to 0.5% of AUM during any future Key Person Event. No further negotiation was required on this point.
>
> \(iv\) **Whitmore Carried Interest Vesting Schedule.** WCA raised concerns regarding the pace of Whitmore\'s residual carried interest vesting, seeking to extend the vesting period from thirty-six (36) months to forty-eight (48) months. After negotiation, the parties agreed to retain the thirty-six (36) month vesting period, subject to a provision that any unvested carried interest would be forfeited if Whitmore were to compete with the Fund (a non-compete carve-out applicable to the vesting period).
>
> \(v\) **GP Fiduciary Obligations During Future Key Person Events.** WCA requested the inclusion of an express statement in the First Amendment confirming the GP\'s ongoing fiduciary obligations to the limited partners during any future Key Person Event. C&H agreed to the inclusion of a confirmatory provision, noting that such obligations already existed under Delaware law and the A&R LPA but acknowledging that an express restatement would provide additional comfort to the LP base.

All negotiated revisions were finalized and incorporated into the execution version of the First Amendment. Graham Sutherland of C&H issued a formal response letter to Helen M. Calloway of WCA, confirming the agreed-upon resolutions and the final form of the First Amendment, on August 5, 2024.

**D. Phase 4: LP Consent Solicitation and Amendment Execution (August 5--26, 2024)**

Following the finalization of the execution version of the First Amendment, DCM redistributed the final form of the First Amendment to all limited partners on August 5, 2024, together with an updated Consent Solicitation Letter reflecting the negotiated revisions. LP consent forms were to be returned to Calderwood & Harkness LLP, Attention: Stephen Adler, at 1585 Broadway, 34th Floor, New York, NY 10036, or by email to the designated matter address.

The consent solicitation period ran from August 5, 2024 through the consent deadline of August 23, 2024. During this period, the C&H engagement team responded to inquiries from limited partners and their counsel regarding the terms of the First Amendment and the consent process, and coordinated with DCM\'s investor relations team to facilitate timely responses to LP due diligence requests.

**August 19, 2024 --- Consent Threshold Met.** As of August 19, 2024, the required LP consent threshold was met and exceeded. Thirty-eight (38) of the Fund\'s forty-seven (47) limited partners delivered executed written consents to C&H, representing aggregate LP capital commitments of \$2,412.8 million. This amount constituted approximately 86.2% of the voting LP commitments of \$2,798.25 million, well in excess of the 66⅔% supermajority threshold of \$1,865.50 million required under Section 8.04(c) of the A&R LPA. The consent threshold was achieved four (4) calendar days in advance of the August 23, 2024 deadline.

**GP Closing Certificate and Consent Tabulation.** C&H prepared the GP Closing Certificate and Consent Tabulation, which set forth a detailed schedule of all LP consents received, the capital commitment represented by each consenting limited partner, and the calculation of the aggregate consenting percentage. The GP Closing Certificate was reviewed and signed by Elaine R. Sato in her capacity as Deputy Chief Investment Officer of DCM, certifying the accuracy of the tabulation and confirming that all conditions precedent to the effectiveness of the First Amendment had been satisfied.

**August 26, 2024 --- First Amendment Effective.** The First Amendment to the A&R LPA became effective on August 26, 2024. The execution version was signed by DCM (by Elaine R. Sato as authorized signatory) and countersigned by the Fund. Copies of the executed First Amendment were delivered to all limited partners, the Investor Advisory Committee, the Fund\'s administrator, auditor, and prime broker, and the Cayman registered agent.

**E. Phase 5: Engagement Closure (August 26--September 2, 2024)**

Following the effectiveness of the First Amendment on August 26, 2024, the C&H engagement team completed all remaining post-closing administrative matters, including the finalization and filing of all matter documents, the delivery of original and copies of executed documents to the appropriate parties, and the confirmation of notifications to Fund service providers. Section 8.04(c) of the A&R LPA further provides that the approval of Successor Key Persons and any related amendments to the A&R LPA shall be subject to the same consent threshold set forth in Section 14.01.

As of the Certification Date, the aggregate Limited Partner capital commitments for purposes of the consent vote (the \"Aggregate Voting LP Capital Commitments\") are calculated as follows:

>

>
> **Aggregate Voting LP Capital Commitments: \$2,798.25 million**

The required consent threshold is therefore:

> \$2,798.25 million × 66⅔% = **\$1,865.50 million**

The standard ERISA representations in the subscription agreement shall be modified accordingly.
>
> \(g\) **Most Favored Nation Election Right.** Right to elect to receive the benefit of any more favorable terms granted to any other limited partner in the Fund (subject to certain Excluded Provisions as described in Section IX of this Checklist), in accordance with the MFN election procedures established in the side letters and the procedures letter to be delivered following the Final Close.

**Item 3: Side Letter --- Brindoval Family Office Holdings LP**

**Description:** Execution copy of the Side Letter (the \"Brindoval Side Letter\") between Pinnacle Venture Capital Management LLC, in its capacity as general partner of Pinnacle Venture Fund II LP, and Brindoval Family Office Holdings LP, dated as of the First Close (January 15, 2026). The Brindoval Side Letter sets forth certain rights, obligations, and modifications to the LPA that are applicable solely as between the General Partner and Brindoval.

**Key Provisions Covered:**

> \(a\) **Opt-Out Rights.** Right of Brindoval to elect not to participate in any Fund investment in a portfolio company that the General Partner determines, in good faith and after consultation with Brindoval, to be directly competitive with any software-as-a-service (\"SaaS\") business owned or controlled by the Raines family or any of its affiliated entities. The General Partner shall provide Brindoval with reasonable prior written notice of any proposed investment that it believes may trigger this opt-out right, together with a summary description of the proposed portfolio company\'s business sufficient for Brindoval to make an informed determination, and shall afford Brindoval a period of not less than ten (10) business days to exercise such right. For the avoidance of doubt, Brindoval\'s exercise of this opt-out right shall not reduce its unfunded commitment to the Fund.
>
> \(b\) **Co-Investment Rights.** Right to participate in co-investment opportunities alongside the Fund on terms consistent with those made available to other co-investment-eligible limited partners, subject to the General Partner\'s discretion regarding allocation.
>
> \(c\) **Management Fee / Carried Interest Netting.** Right to have management fees paid by Brindoval netted against distributions of carried interest otherwise payable to the General Partner with respect to Brindoval\'s interest in the Fund. This netting mechanism applies at the time of each distribution and effectively reduces the General Partner\'s carried interest allocation attributable to Brindoval\'s interest by the aggregate amount of management fees previously paid by Brindoval.
>
> \(d\) **Information Rights.** Entitlement to enhanced information rights aligned with the Institutional Limited Partners Association (\"ILPA\") best practices, including (i) annual audited financial statements delivered within 90 days following the end of each fiscal year, (ii) unaudited quarterly financial statements delivered within 45 days following the end of each fiscal quarter, (iii) capital account statements, and (iv) annual meeting or investor update access.
>
> \(e\) **Most Favored Nation Election Right.** Right to elect to receive the benefit of any more favorable terms granted to any other limited partner in the Fund (subject to certain Excluded Provisions as described in Section IX of this Checklist), in accordance with the MFN election procedures established in the side letters and the procedures letter to be delivered following the Final Close.
>
> \(f\) **Management Fee Rate.** Standard management fee of 2.00% per annum on committed capital during the Investment Period (no discount from the standard rate set forth in Section 6.1 of the LPA). Post-Investment Period management fee at the standard rate of 2.00% per annum on invested capital.

**Commitment Amount:** \$40,000,000

**Responsible Party:** C&H (prepare final execution version); GP (execute on behalf of the Fund); LP Counsel --- Prescott & Langley LLP (Angela Ferris) (obtain LP execution)

**Number of Originals Required:** Two (2) --- one original for the General Partner\'s files and one original for Brindoval\'s files.

**Status:** \[   \]

**Date Last Updated:** **\_\_\_**

\(c\) If the General Partner does not exercise the ROFR within the GP ROFR Period, the General Partner shall promptly notify the other Limited Partners, and the other Limited Partners shall have a further period of fifteen (15) days following receipt of such notice (the \"**LP ROFR Period**\") to elect, by written notice to the General Partner and the transferring Limited Partner, to purchase the offered Partnership Interest (or such portion thereof as is offered), pro rata based on their respective Partnership Percentages (calculated without regard to the transferring Limited Partner\'s Partnership Percentage). If more than one non-transferring Limited Partner elects to purchase and the aggregate elections exceed the offered Partnership Interest, such elections shall be satisfied pro rata based on the electing Limited Partners\' respective Partnership Percentages.

\(d\) If neither the General Partner nor the other Limited Partners exercise the ROFR within the applicable periods, the transferring Limited Partner may, subject to satisfaction of all other conditions in Section 8.2, consummate the Transfer to the proposed transferee identified in the Transfer Notice, at the same price and on terms no more favorable to the transferee than those set forth in the Transfer Notice, within sixty (60) days following the expiration of the LP ROFR Period. If the Transfer is not consummated within such sixty (60)-day period, the ROFR process set forth in this Section 8.3 must be repeated before any Transfer may occur.

**Section 8.4 --- Transfers by the General Partner**

The General Partner shall not Transfer its general partner interest in the Partnership without the prior written consent of Limited Partners holding a majority-in-interest of the aggregate Capital Commitments of all Limited Partners; provided, however, that the General Partner may, without the consent of the Limited Partners, Transfer its general partner interest to an Affiliate of the General Partner or Ridgeline Management, provided that (i) such Affiliate assumes all obligations of the General Partner hereunder, (ii) such Affiliate is wholly owned, directly or indirectly, by Ridgeline Management, and (iii) the General Partner provides at least ten (10) Business Days\' prior written notice to the Limited Partners of such Transfer.

**Section 8.5 --- Tag-Along Rights**

\(a\) If Fund IV proposes to Transfer all or any portion of its interest in AcquisitionCo to a third party that is not an Affiliate of Fund IV or Fund IV GP (a \"**Tag-Along Sale**\"), each Limited Partner shall have the right (a \"**Tag-Along Right**\") to participate in such Transfer on a pro rata basis, at the same price per unit of AcquisitionCo Equity and on the same terms and conditions as Fund IV.

\(b\) The General Partner shall provide at least twenty (20) Business Days\' prior written notice to each Limited Partner of any proposed Tag-Along Sale (a \"**Tag-Along Notice**\"), which notice shall set forth the identity of the proposed purchaser, the proposed price, and the material terms and conditions of the proposed sale.

\(c\) Each Limited Partner may elect to exercise its Tag-Along Right by delivering written notice to the General Partner within fifteen (15) Business Days of receipt of the Tag-Along Notice. Any Limited Partner that does not deliver a timely election notice shall be deemed to have waived its Tag-Along Right with respect to such Tag-Along Sale.

\(d\) Each Limited Partner exercising its Tag-Along Right may include in such Tag-Along Sale up to one hundred percent (100%) of its proportionate interest in the AcquisitionCo Equity (determined based on the Partnership\'s proportionate ownership of AcquisitionCo and such Limited Partner\'s Partnership Percentage).

\(e\) The closing of any Tag-Along Sale shall be conditioned upon the participation of all Limited Partners that have timely exercised their Tag-Along Rights.

**Section 8.6 --- Drag-Along Rights**

\(a\) If the General Partner determines, in its sole discretion, to sell one hundred percent (100%) of the AcquisitionCo Equity held by the Partnership and Fund IV to a third party (a \"**Drag-Along Sale**\"), the General Partner may require all Limited Partners to sell their proportionate interests in the AcquisitionCo Equity (indirectly, through the Partnership) on the same terms and conditions as Fund IV (the \"**Drag-Along Right**\").

\(b\) The General Partner shall provide at least twenty (20) Business Days\' prior written notice to each Limited Partner of any proposed Drag-Along Sale (a \"**Drag-Along Notice**\"), which notice shall set forth the identity of the proposed purchaser, the proposed price, and the material terms and conditions of the proposed sale.

\(c\) In any Drag-Along Sale, each Limited Partner shall receive its proportionate share of the sale proceeds in accordance with the Distribution waterfall set forth in Section 6.2.

\(d\) In connection with any Drag-Along Sale, the representations and warranties required of the dragged Limited Partners shall be limited to (i) title to and ownership of their Partnership Interests, (ii) authority and power to enter into and perform the sale transaction, and (iii) the absence of encumbrances on their Partnership Interests. No Limited Partner shall be required to make any representations or warranties with respect to the business, assets, liabilities, operations, or financial condition of AcquisitionCo, Clarion, or any of their respective subsidiaries.

\(e\) Each Limited Partner hereby agrees to take all actions and execute all documents reasonably requested by the General Partner to consummate a Drag-Along Sale, including execution of purchase agreements, closing certificates, and related instruments.

**Section 8.7 --- Substitute Limited Partners**

A permitted transferee of a Partnership Interest shall be admitted to the Partnership as a substitute Limited Partner only upon satisfaction of all conditions set forth in Section 8.2 and execution and delivery of such documentation as the General Partner may reasonably require, including a joinder agreement substantially in the form of Exhibit A. Upon admission as a substitute Limited Partner, the transferee shall succeed to all of the rights and obligations of the transferring Limited Partner with respect to the transferred Partnership Interest, and the transferring Limited Partner shall be released from all obligations hereunder with respect to the transferred Partnership Interest (other than obligations that accrued prior to the effective date of such Transfer). The General Partner shall promptly update Schedule A to reflect any such substitution.

**[ARTICLE IX --- LIMITED PARTNER ADVISORY COMMITTEE (LPAC)]{.underline}**

**Section 9.1 --- Establishment and Composition**

The Partnership shall establish a Limited Partner Advisory Committee (the \"**LPAC**\") consisting of three (3) members. The members of the LPAC shall be appointed by the General Partner from among the Limited Partners or their designated representatives; provided, however, that Pellegrino Capital Group LLC shall be entitled to appoint one (1) member of the LPAC for so long as Pellegrino Capital Group LLC holds a Partnership Interest in the Partnership. LPAC members shall serve in a non-fiduciary, advisory capacity, except where specific approval or consent rights are expressly conferred upon the LPAC by this Agreement. For the avoidance of doubt, LPAC members shall not owe any fiduciary duties to the Partnership or to any other Partner by virtue of their service on the LPAC.

**Section 9.2 --- LPAC Functions**

The LPAC shall have the following functions and responsibilities:

\(a\) Review and approve (or disapprove) conflict transactions between the Partnership and the General Partner or any of its Affiliates as contemplated by Section 7.3(c);

\(b\) Review and approve (or disapprove) all other matters requiring LPAC consent as set forth in Section 7.3;

\(c\) Consult with the General Partner regarding valuations of the Investment, including the methodology and inputs used for such valuations;

\(d\) Review and approve (or disapprove) any proposed Distributions in kind pursuant to Section 6.7;

\(e\) Consult with the General Partner regarding the management transition plan in connection with a Key Person Event pursuant to Section 10.1; and

\(f\) Perform such other advisory functions as the General Partner may request from time to time, including review of the Partnership\'s annual financial statements and consultation on material strategic matters relating to the Investment.

**Section 9.3 --- LPAC Meetings**

\(a\) The LPAC shall meet at least once per calendar year, or more frequently as the General Partner or any two (2) LPAC members may request. Meetings may be held in person at the offices of the General Partner, by video conference, or by telephonic conference, as determined by the General Partner in consultation with the LPAC members.

\(b\) The General Partner shall provide at least ten (10) Business Days\' prior written notice of each meeting to all LPAC members, together with a written agenda and copies of any relevant materials to be discussed at such meeting.

\(c\) A quorum for any meeting of the LPAC shall consist of a majority of the LPAC members (i.e., two (2) of three (3) members). Actions of the LPAC shall be taken by the affirmative vote or written consent of a majority of the LPAC members (i.e., two (2) of three (3) members).

\(d\) Actions may be taken by the LPAC without a meeting by written consent signed by a majority of the LPAC members, which consent shall be effective as of the date of the last signature.

\(e\) The General Partner shall prepare and distribute to all LPAC members written minutes of each meeting within fifteen (15) Business Days following such meeting.

**Section 9.4 --- Indemnification of LPAC Members**

Each member of the LPAC shall be indemnified by the Partnership on the same basis as Covered Persons under Section 7.9 with respect to any Losses incurred by such member arising out of or in connection with such member\'s service on the LPAC. LPAC members acting in good faith in the performance of their duties as LPAC members shall have no personal liability to the Partnership, the General Partner, or any Limited Partner for any actions taken or omitted to be taken in their advisory capacity as LPAC members.

**Section 9.5 --- Removal and Replacement**

\(a\) The General Partner may remove any LPAC member for Cause upon written notice to such LPAC member and the Limited Partner that appointed or designated such member.

\(b\) Any Limited Partner that appointed or designated an LPAC member may, at any time, designate a replacement for such LPAC member by written notice to the General Partner, and such replacement shall become effective upon receipt of such notice by the General Partner.

\(c\) In the event of a vacancy on the LPAC (whether by removal, resignation, or otherwise), the General Partner shall appoint a replacement LPAC member from among the Limited Partners or their designated representatives within thirty (30) days of such vacancy; provided, however, that any vacancy in the LPAC seat held by a designee of Pellegrino Capital Group LLC shall be filled by a designee of Pellegrino Capital Group LLC.

=====  documents/matters/1023-00001/Formation/formation-governance-summary-memo.docx =====
This memorandum has been prepared by Calderwood & Harkness LLP ("C&H" or the "Firm") for the internal files of Ironside Capital Management LP ("Ironside" or "ICM") to provide a comprehensive summary of the formation steps completed to date and the governance structure of ICM Cascadia Co-Invest, LP (the "Vehicle" or the "Partnership"), a Delaware limited partnership formed for the purpose of co-investing alongside Meridian Infrastructure Partners Fund IV, LP ("Fund IV") in the acquisition of 100% of the outstanding equity interests of Cascadia Renewables Holdings, Inc. ("Cascadia" or "CRH"), an Oregon corporation.
The Vehicle has been organized as a single-purpose, single-limited-partner co-investment vehicle designed to facilitate Ironside's participation in the Cascadia acquisition on terms that are more favorable to Ironside than those applicable to Fund IV's general limited partner base. Specifically, the Vehicle was formed to commit Three Hundred Million Dollars ($300,000,000) to the acquisition, representing approximately 28.57% of the total equity commitment of One Billion Fifty Million Dollars ($1,050,000,000). Fund IV is committing the remaining Seven Hundred Fifty Million Dollars ($750,000,000), representing approximately 71.43% of the total equity commitment.
The Certificate of Limited Partnership of ICM Cascadia Co-Invest, LP was prepared by C&H and filed with the Delaware Secretary of State on July 22, 2022. The filing was accepted and processed on the same date, and the Partnership's legal existence commenced upon such filing in accordance with Section 17-201 of the Delaware Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act ("DRULPA"), 6 Del. C. §§ 17-101 et seq.
The Certificate of Limited Partnership is in the standard form prescribed by DRULPA Section 17-201 and contains the name of the Partnership, the address of the registered office in Delaware, the name and address of the registered agent, and the name and address of the general partner. A certified copy of the Certificate of Limited Partnership has been obtained from the Delaware Secretary of State and is retained in the Firm's deal files.
In addition to the Certificate of Limited Partnership and the LP Agreement, the following ancillary formation and transaction documents have been prepared and are either executed or scheduled for execution:
2. Co-Investment Allocation Agreement. A co-investment allocation agreement (the "Co-Investment Allocation Agreement") between Meridian Infrastructure Partners Fund IV, LP (Fund IV) and ICM Cascadia Co-Invest, LP (the Vehicle) has been negotiated and is in final form. The Co-Investment Allocation Agreement governs the allocation of the co-investment between Fund IV and the Vehicle, establishing the 28.57% (Vehicle) / 71.43% (Fund IV) pro rata split and the parallel investment mechanics applicable to the Cascadia acquisition. The Co-Investment Allocation Agreement ensures that Fund IV and the Vehicle participate in the acquisition on a pari passu basis, with proportionate economics, voting rights, and information rights at the portfolio-company level.
5. Placement Agent Agreement. Rivermark Capital Markets Inc. ("Rivermark") has been engaged as the placement agent for the Vehicle pursuant to a placement agent agreement executed between Meridian Infrastructure GP IV LLC and Rivermark. The placement agent fee is 0.35% of committed capital, resulting in a fee of One Million Fifty Thousand Dollars ($1,050,000), payable at first close. C&H has reviewed the placement agent agreement and provided its analysis in a separate memorandum dated July 18, 2022.
1.  Execution of Transaction Documents. The LP Agreement, Side Letter, Subscription Agreement, and Co-Investment Allocation Agreement are anticipated to be executed by all parties on July 29, 2022, at first close.
2.  First Capital Call. The first capital call under the LP Agreement is anticipated for mid-August 2022. Based on preliminary estimates, the first capital call is expected to be approximately 7.5% of committed capital, or approximately $22,500,000, to fund organizational expenses, the placement-agent fee, the representations and warranties insurance premium deposit, due-diligence costs and deposits, and the working-capital reserve.
The Partnership has two partners: the General Partner and the Limited Partner. The Vehicle is structured as a single-LP co-investment vehicle with no additional limited partners anticipated.
Meridian Infrastructure GP IV LLC serves as the sole general partner of the Partnership. The General Partner is a Delaware limited liability company organized for the purpose of serving as the general partner of Fund IV and its related co-investment vehicles, including the Vehicle. The key details of the General Partner are as follows:
The Vehicle is structured as a single-LP co-investment vehicle. No additional limited partners are anticipated, and the admission of any additional limited partners would require the prior written consent of the existing Limited Partner (Ironside) pursuant to Section 5.01 of the LP Agreement.
The economic terms of the Vehicle have been negotiated to reflect the co-investment nature of the arrangement and are significantly more favorable to Ironside than the standard economic terms applicable to Fund IV's main limited partnership. The key economic terms are summarized below:
Management Fee. No management fee (0%) is charged on the Vehicle. The Side Letter expressly confirms that no management fee, monitoring fee, or similar ongoing fee is payable by the Partnership to the General Partner or any of its affiliates in connection with the Vehicle. This is a material economic benefit to Ironside, as Fund IV's main limited partnership is subject to a management fee of 2% per annum on committed capital during the investment period and 2% per annum on invested capital thereafter.
Carried Interest. The General Partner is entitled to a carried interest of 10% of net profits above the preferred return, as compared to the 20% carried interest applicable in Fund IV's main limited partnership. The reduced carried interest rate reflects the co-investment nature of the Vehicle and Ironside's significant capital commitment. The carried interest is subject to the distribution waterfall mechanics described in Section XI of this memorandum.
The sole purpose of the Partnership, as set forth in Section 2.01 of the LP Agreement, is to co-invest alongside Fund IV in the acquisition of 100% of the outstanding equity interests of Cascadia Renewables Holdings, Inc. through Cascadia Acquisition Corp., a Delaware corporation to be formed as the acquisition subsidiary. Cascadia Acquisition Corp. will be wholly owned, directly or indirectly, by Fund IV and the Vehicle in proportion to their respective equity commitments (71.43% Fund IV / 28.57% Vehicle).
The Vehicle's co-investment percentage of total equity is 28.57%, calculated as $300,000,000 divided by $1,050,000,000 in total equity commitments. The Co-Investment Allocation Agreement governs the allocation mechanics and ensures parallel treatment of Fund IV and the Vehicle throughout the life of the investment.
Pursuant to Section 3.01 of the LP Agreement, the General Partner has exclusive authority to manage and control the business and affairs of the Partnership. This broad grant of authority is consistent with the default rules under DRULPA and with customary market practice for sponsor-led co-investment vehicles. Specifically, the General Partner's authority includes, without limitation, the following:
(f) enter into any related-party transaction (including any transaction with the General Partner, its affiliates, Fund IV, or their respective principals, officers, or employees) that is not expressly contemplated by the LP Agreement or the Co-Investment Allocation Agreement; and
These consent requirements are designed to protect Ironside's interests as the sole limited partner and to ensure that the General Partner does not take any material action that could adversely affect Ironside's investment without Ironside's knowledge and approval. The consent requirements are consistent with market practice for single-LP co-investment vehicles and reflect the negotiated balance of authority between the General Partner and the Limited Partner.
C. LP Advisory Committee
No formal Limited Partner Advisory Committee ("LPAC") is established under the LP Agreement. The absence of a formal LPAC is appropriate given the single-LP structure of the Vehicle — there is no need for a committee to represent the interests of multiple limited partners, as Ironside is the sole limited partner and has direct consent rights on all material matters.
In lieu of a formal LPAC, the Side Letter provides for direct consultation between the General Partner and Ironside on material matters affecting the Partnership and its investment. The GP has agreed to consult with Ironside in good faith on matters that would customarily be brought before an LPAC in a multi-investor fund, including conflict-of-interest matters, related-party transactions, valuation issues, and material deviations from the investment thesis.
The Co-Investment Allocation Agreement governs the parallel investment mechanics between Fund IV and the Vehicle, ensuring that both entities participate in the acquisition and all subsequent investment decisions on a pro rata basis (28.57% Vehicle / 71.43% Fund IV). The Co-Investment Allocation Agreement provides for parallel economic treatment, meaning that Fund IV and the Vehicle receive the same terms with respect to the acquisition, any subsequent investments, and the ultimate disposition of the investment, subject to differences in their respective economic terms (e.g., the Vehicle's lower carried interest rate).
Any deviation from the pro rata allocation set forth in the Co-Investment Allocation Agreement requires the prior written consent of the Limited Partner (Ironside). This provision protects Ironside against dilution or adverse reallocation of investment economics as between Fund IV and the Vehicle.
Duty of Care. The duty of care owed by the General Partner is limited to a "gross negligence or willful misconduct" standard. Under this standard, the General Partner is not liable to the Partnership or any partner for errors in judgment, losses, or other adverse outcomes arising from its management of the Partnership's affairs, unless such errors, losses, or outcomes result from the General Partner's gross negligence, willful misconduct, fraud, or bad faith. This modification is consistent with the standard of care commonly adopted in Delaware limited partnership agreements for private equity and infrastructure funds and is permissible under DRULPA Section 17-1101(d).
Duty of Loyalty. The duty of loyalty owed by the General Partner is preserved but is qualified to account for the General Partner's role as the sponsor of Fund IV and other investment vehicles. Specifically, the LP Agreement provides that the General Partner and its affiliates (including Meridian and Fund IV) may engage in other business activities, including activities that compete with or are similar to the Partnership's business, without any obligation to account to the Partnership for any profits or benefits derived from such activities. This qualification is necessary to accommodate the General Partner's role as the general partner of Fund IV and its other investment activities, and the specific allocation as between Fund IV and the Vehicle is governed by the Co-Investment Allocation Agreement.
B. Exculpation
The LP Agreement includes a customary exculpation provision that limits the personal liability of the General Partner and certain related persons in connection with the Partnership's activities. Specifically, the General Partner and its affiliates, managers, members, officers, and employees (collectively, the "Covered Persons") are exculpated from liability to the Partnership or the Limited Partner for any act or omission taken or suffered in good faith and reasonably believed by the applicable Covered Person to be within the scope of the authority conferred by the LP Agreement, except to the extent that such act or omission constitutes gross negligence, willful misconduct, fraud, or bad faith.
The exculpation provision is drafted broadly to cover the full range of activities that the Covered Persons may undertake in connection with the Partnership's business, including investment decisions, operational decisions, service provider engagement, and all other actions taken in the course of managing the Partnership's affairs. The carve-outs for gross negligence, willful misconduct, fraud, and bad faith ensure that the Covered Persons remain accountable for egregious conduct while providing appropriate protection against liability for good-faith errors in judgment.
The LP Agreement provides for indemnification of the Covered Persons by the Partnership against losses, damages, liabilities, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees and expenses) arising out of or in connection with the Partnership's activities. The indemnification obligation is subject to the same carve-outs applicable to the exculpation provision — indemnification is not available to the extent that the conduct giving rise to the claim constitutes gross negligence, willful misconduct, fraud, or bad faith.
The fiduciary duty, exculpation, and indemnification provisions of the LP Agreement have been drafted in accordance with the requirements and limitations of DRULPA. Several provisions of DRULPA are particularly relevant:
DRULPA § 17-1101(d). This section provides that a limited partnership agreement may modify, restrict, or expand the fiduciary duties owed by a partner or other person to the partnership or to another partner. The statute expressly permits the elimination of fiduciary duties, subject to the limitation that a partnership agreement may not eliminate the implied contractual covenant of good faith and fair dealing.
Implied Covenant of Good Faith and Fair Dealing. In accordance with DRULPA Section 17-1101(d), the LP Agreement expressly preserves the implied contractual covenant of good faith and fair dealing. This covenant provides a baseline level of protection for the Limited Partner against arbitrary or opportunistic conduct by the General Partner, even in areas where the LP Agreement has modified or limited the General Partner's fiduciary duties. Delaware courts have consistently held that the implied covenant serves as a gap-filling mechanism to address situations not expressly covered by the partnership agreement, and the preservation of this covenant in the LP Agreement is both appropriate and consistent with best practices.
The LP Agreement does not provide for the removal of the General Partner without cause. The absence of a no-fault removal right is a common feature in co-investment vehicles where the General Partner is the sponsor of the main fund (here, Fund IV). The rationale for this approach is that the General Partner's role in managing the co-investment is closely tied to its role in managing the main fund, and removal of the General Partner from the co-investment vehicle without cause could create governance and operational complexities for the broader investment program.
The LP Agreement provides the Limited Partner (Ironside) with comprehensive information rights that are designed to ensure that Ironside has timely and complete access to information regarding the Partnership's financial condition, investment status, and material developments. The LP's information rights under the LP Agreement include the following:
Capital Call Notices. The General Partner is required to provide at least ten (10) business days' prior written notice to the Limited Partner of any capital call. Each capital call notice must specify the amount of the capital call, the purpose for which the capital is being called (including a reasonably detailed description of the anticipated uses of the called capital), and the due date for payment.
(b) Books and Records Access. The Limited Partner has the right to access and review the General Partner's books and records relating to the Partnership upon reasonable prior written notice to the General Partner. This right is in addition to the statutory right of inspection provided under DRULPA Section 17-305.
The Limited Partner has the right to inspect and copy the books and records of the Partnership during normal business hours upon reasonable prior written notice to the General Partner. This right is consistent with the statutory right of inspection provided under DRULPA Section 17-305, which grants limited partners the right, for any purpose reasonably related to the limited partner's interest, to inspect and copy specified partnership records.
The Material Impediment Event provisions are designed to provide a structured framework for addressing significant obstacles to the Cascadia acquisition, including regulatory delays, financing disruptions, adverse changes in the target's business, and other events that could prevent or materially delay the closing of the transaction.
(d) The Partnership files a Certificate of Cancellation with the Delaware Secretary of State in accordance with DRULPA Section 17-203, formally terminating the Partnership's legal existence.
(a) the entry of a decree of judicial dissolution under DRULPA Section 17-802;
The distribution waterfall is structured as a standard "whole fund" or "European-style" waterfall, in which the preferred return must be fully satisfied before any carried interest is payable to the General Partner. The 10% carried interest rate compares favorably to the 20% carried interest applicable in Fund IV's main limited partnership and reflects the negotiated economics of the co-investment arrangement.
These transfer restrictions are designed to preserve the integrity of the partnership structure and to ensure that neither party may unilaterally introduce a new partner or alter the governance dynamics of the Vehicle without the consent of the other party.
1.  Execution of Transaction Documents. The LP Agreement, Side Letter, Co-Investment Allocation Agreement, and Subscription Agreement are anticipated to be executed by all parties on July 29, 2022, at first close.
Please do not hesitate to contact the undersigned or any member of the Calderwood & Harkness team with questions regarding this memorandum or any aspect of the Vehicle's formation and governance.

**CALDERWOOD & HARKNESS LLP** *Counselors at Law* One Vanderbilt Avenue, 44th Floor New York, New York 10017

Telephone: (212) 814-6000 Facsimile: (212) 814-6001 www.calderwoodharkness.com

October 9, 2023

**VIA EMAIL AND HAND DELIVERY**

Ardent Capital Management LLC 590 Madison Avenue, 28th Floor New York, New York 10022

> Attention: Marcus Aldridge, Co-Founder & Managing Partner
>
> Priya Narayanan, Co-Founder & Managing Partner

Dear Mr. Aldridge and Ms. Narayanan:

We are pleased to confirm the engagement of Calderwood & Harkness LLP (\"Calderwood & Harkness,\" the \"Firm,\" \"we,\" or \"us\") by Ardent Capital Management LLC (the \"ManCo\" or the \"Client\") to serve as legal counsel in connection with the matters described herein. This letter (the \"Engagement Letter\") sets forth the terms and conditions upon which we will provide legal services to the Client in connection with this engagement.

**[1. Purpose and Engagement]{.underline}**

This Engagement Letter confirms that Calderwood & Harkness has been engaged by the ManCo to serve as legal counsel in connection with a comprehensive restructuring of the management company and realignment of economics among the principals of Ardent Capital Partners III LP (the \"Fund\"), a Delaware limited partnership with approximately \$2.8 billion in total commitments. The ManCo is a Delaware limited liability company and a registered investment adviser with the United States Securities and Exchange Commission (the \"SEC\") under CRD #298417. The Fund\'s sole general partner is Ardent Capital GP III LLC (the \"General Partner\"), a Delaware limited liability company.

The engagement encompasses the formation of new holding entities, the negotiation of separation arrangements with departing principals, the realignment of carried interest and management fee economics among continuing and next-generation principals, the solicitation of necessary limited partner consents, compliance with existing side-letter obligations, and related tax structuring. The scope of the representation, the personnel assigned to the engagement, the fee arrangement, and other terms and conditions governing this engagement are set forth in the sections that follow.

**[2. Scope of Representation]{.underline}**

The engagement will comprise the following principal workstreams, each of which is described in greater detail below. We understand that the scope of the engagement may evolve as the restructuring progresses; any material expansion of the scope described herein will be discussed with the Client in advance.

**2.1 Entity Restructuring**

Calderwood & Harkness will advise on the restructuring of the organizational hierarchy of the Ardent Capital platform, including:

\(a\) Advising on the formation of a new Delaware limited liability company, to be named Ardent Capital Holdings LLC (\"HoldCo\"), which will serve as a parent holding company for both the General Partner and the ManCo, thereby consolidating the principals\' economic interests and governance rights in a single vehicle at the top of the organizational structure.

\(b\) Advising on the formation of an intermediate entity, Ardent GP Intermediate LLC (\"GP Intermediate\"), as a wholly owned subsidiary of HoldCo and the sole member of the General Partner. GP Intermediate will serve as an interposing entity between HoldCo and the General Partner, facilitating the allocation of carried interest economics and providing structural flexibility for the admission of future principals and the potential establishment of successor funds.

\(c\) Drafting and negotiating limited liability company agreements for each of HoldCo and GP Intermediate, including provisions governing capital contributions, profit and loss allocations, distribution waterfalls, governance (including voting and consent requirements), transfer restrictions, withdrawal and removal mechanics, non-compete and non-solicitation covenants, and such other provisions as may be appropriate.

\(d\) Preparing amended and restated limited liability company agreements for the General Partner and the ManCo to reflect the new holding-company structure, including modifications to membership interest provisions, management and officer provisions, and capital account and allocation provisions necessitated by the interposition of HoldCo and GP Intermediate.

\(e\) Preparing and filing Certificates of Formation with the Delaware Secretary of State for each of HoldCo and GP Intermediate, together with any ancillary filings or registrations required in connection with the formation and qualification of such entities.

\(f\) Preparing Amendment No. 1 to the Amended and Restated Agreement of Limited Partnership of the Fund (the \"LPA\") to reflect the structural changes to the General Partner, including any required modifications to the definitions, representations, and governance provisions of the LPA necessitated by the interposition of GP Intermediate and HoldCo above the General Partner.

**2.2 Economics Realignment**

Calderwood & Harkness will advise on the reallocation and documentation of the economic arrangements among the principals of the Fund, including:

\(a\) Advising on the reallocation of carried interest percentages and management fee profit-share allocations among the remaining and next-generation principals, taking into account the departure of the principals described in Section 2.3 below, the contributions of continuing principals, and the Firm\'s understanding of the Client\'s objectives with respect to the incentivization and retention of key personnel.

\(b\) Drafting an amended and restated Carried Interest Allocation Agreement reflecting the revised carried interest percentages applicable to each principal, including vesting schedules, forfeiture and clawback provisions, and mechanics for the allocation of carried interest among HoldCo members through the GP Intermediate and General Partner chain.

\(c\) Drafting a Management Fee Sharing and Profit Allocation Agreement at the HoldCo level, setting forth the allocation of management fee revenue among HoldCo members, including base compensation allocations, discretionary bonus pools, and distribution priorities.

\(d\) Revising the co-investment allocation policy to reflect the revised principal group and to address any changes in co-investment rights and priorities resulting from the restructuring.

**2.3 Departing Principal Separation**

Calderwood & Harkness will advise on the negotiation and documentation of separation arrangements for two departing principals:

\(a\) **David Kellner** (Senior Partner), who is retiring from the Ardent Capital platform; and

\(b\) **Joanna Trask** (Partner), who is departing voluntarily.

In connection with each departing principal, the Firm will:

> \(i\) Draft comprehensive separation and release agreements, addressing, among other things, the departing principal\'s resignation from all positions with the ManCo, the General Partner, HoldCo (if applicable), and all affiliated entities; mutual releases of claims; confidentiality, non-disparagement, non-solicitation, and (as applicable) non-competition covenants; cooperation obligations; and any ongoing compensation or benefits arrangements.
>
> \(ii\) Draft carry retention and clawback side letters, specifying the portion of carried interest to be retained by each departing principal with respect to investments made during his or her tenure, the clawback obligations applicable thereto, and the mechanics for the calculation and payment of any retained carry distributions.
>
> \(iii\) As applicable, draft a senior advisor agreement in favor of Mr. Kellner, setting forth the terms of any ongoing advisory role, including the scope of services, compensation, expense reimbursement, and termination provisions.
>
> \(iv\) Coordinate, as necessary and appropriate, with Whitford & Chase LLP, counsel to the departing principals, led by Richard Beaulieu, Esq., in connection with the negotiation and finalization of all separation documentation.

**2.4 LP Consent and Side-Letter Compliance**

Calderwood & Harkness will advise on all limited partner notification, consent, and compliance matters arising from the restructuring, including:

\(a\) Preparing materials for notification to, and solicitation of consent from, the Limited Partner Advisory Committee (\"LPAC\") pursuant to Section 9.4 of the LPA, including a detailed memorandum describing the restructuring and its implications for the Fund and its limited partners.

\(b\) Analyzing compliance with the Fund\'s fourteen (14) existing side letters, with particular attention to key-person provisions under Section 5.2 of the LPA and any expanded or supplemental key-person provisions contained in certain side letters, to determine whether the departures of Mr. Kellner and Ms. Trask or the structural changes contemplated by the restructuring trigger key-person events, consent requirements, or notification obligations under any such side letter.

\(c\) Preparing LP notification letters to all forty-seven (47) limited partners of the Fund, describing the restructuring, the changes to the General Partner structure, the departures of Mr. Kellner and Ms. Trask, and any other information required to be disclosed under the LPA or the applicable side letters.

\(d\) Advising on the preparation and filing of an amended SEC Form ADV (Parts 1 and 2) to reflect the restructuring, and advising on any other regulatory filings or notifications required in connection with the restructuring, including any applicable state regulatory filings.

**2.5 Tax Structuring**

Calderwood & Harkness will provide tax analysis and structuring advice in connection with the restructuring, including:

\(a\) Federal income tax analysis of the formation of HoldCo and GP Intermediate, including the tax treatment of the contribution or transfer of interests in the General Partner and the ManCo to HoldCo.

\(b\) Delaware tax analysis of the formation of HoldCo and GP Intermediate, including any applicable Delaware franchise taxes, formation taxes, or annual reporting obligations.

\(c\) Federal income tax analysis of the reallocation of carried interest among the principals, including the application of Section 1061 of the Internal Revenue Code and any implications arising from the modification of existing partnership interests.

\(d\) Tax analysis of the economic arrangements with departing principals, including the characterization of carry retention payments and the tax treatment of any consideration paid in connection with the separation arrangements.

\(e\) Section 704(b) and Section 704(c) analysis of built-in gain allocations with respect to existing Fund investments, including the impact of the restructuring on the allocation of built-in gains and losses among the principals and the mechanics for tracking and allocating such amounts through the revised entity structure.

\(f\) All tax structuring advice under this engagement will be provided by Sylvia Hartwell, Specialist Partner (Tax), who will coordinate as necessary with the Client\'s independent accountants at Heathrow Whitman & Co.

**2.6 Limitations on Scope**

The scope of this engagement is limited to the matters described in Sections 2.1 through 2.5 above. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, the following matters are expressly excluded from the scope of this engagement:

\(a\) Routine fund operations, portfolio company transactions, and ongoing limited partner communications unrelated to the restructuring described herein. We understand that such matters will continue to be handled by Pemberton Hale LLP (Victoria Langford, Partner), which serves as the Fund\'s existing fund formation and operations counsel.

\(b\) Accounting, auditing, and valuation services, which we understand are provided by Heathrow Whitman & Co. (accountants and auditors) and Broadleaf Consulting Group (valuation), respectively. Nothing in this engagement shall be construed as the provision of accounting, auditing, or valuation advice by Calderwood & Harkness.

\(c\) Representation of any departing principal, including David Kellner and Joanna Trask, in connection with the restructuring or any other matter. Each departing principal is separately represented by Whitford & Chase LLP.

\(d\) Representation of any limited partner of the Fund in connection with the restructuring or any other matter.

To the extent matters arise during the course of this engagement that fall outside the scope described herein but that may benefit from our involvement, we will discuss with the Client whether and on what terms such matters should be added to the scope of this engagement or addressed through a separate engagement.

**[3. Engagement Team]{.underline}**

The following attorneys will serve as the primary members of the engagement team:

  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Name**                **Role**                   **Responsibility**
  ----------------------- -------------------------- -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Nicholas Stern          Responsible Partner        Overall supervision of the engagement, strategic advice, and senior-level involvement in key negotiations and decision points

  Graham Sutherland       Billing Partner            Billing, engagement administration, and fee-related communications

  Owen Fischer            Lead Associate             Day-to-day management of the engagement, including document drafting and negotiation, coordination with counterparty counsel (Whitford & Chase LLP) and other advisors (Pemberton Hale LLP, Heathrow Whitman & Co., Broadleaf Consulting Group)

  Stephen Adler           Working Associate          Document drafting, due diligence, preparation of regulatory filings, and research support

  Sylvia Hartwell         Specialist Partner (Tax)   Tax structuring advice, Section 704(b) and 704(c) analysis, and coordination with Heathrow Whitman & Co. on tax-related matters
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

From time to time, additional attorneys or paraprofessionals may be assigned to the engagement as the Firm deems necessary or appropriate to ensure efficient and timely completion of the workstreams described herein. The Client will be notified in advance of any such additions to the engagement team.

**[4. Fee Arrangement and Billing]{.underline}**

**4.1 Hourly Rates**

Fees for services rendered in connection with this engagement will be charged on an hourly basis at the following standard rates:

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Timekeeper Level**                **Hourly Rate**
  ----------------------------------- -----------------------------------
  Partner                             \$1,650

  Specialist Partner                  \$1,750

  Senior Associate                    \$950

  Associate                           \$750
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------

The foregoing rates are subject to annual adjustment, typically effective January 1 of each year. In the event of any rate adjustment during the term of this engagement, the Firm will communicate such adjustment to the Client in advance. Adjusted rates will apply to services rendered on or after the effective date of the adjustment.

**4.2 Estimated Fee Range**

Based on the anticipated scope and complexity of the engagement as described in Section 2 above, and taking into account the number of workstreams, the anticipated volume of document drafting and negotiation, and the extent of LP consent and regulatory compliance work expected to be required, we estimate that total professional fees for this engagement will fall within the range of **\$850,000 to \$1,100,000**.

This estimate is provided solely for budgeting purposes and does not constitute a cap, ceiling, or fixed fee. Actual fees may vary from this estimate based on a number of factors, including (without limitation) the ultimate scope and complexity of the work, the nature and duration of negotiations with Whitford & Chase LLP on behalf of the departing principals, the extent and complexity of LP consent solicitation and side-letter compliance matters, the number and complexity of tax structuring issues that arise, and any expansion of the scope of the engagement beyond the matters described herein. The Firm will endeavor to keep the Client informed on an ongoing basis of any circumstances that are likely to cause total fees to exceed the upper end of the estimated range, and will discuss with the Client any potential modifications to the scope or approach to the engagement that might mitigate such costs.

**4.3 Disbursements.** In addition to professional fees, the Client will be responsible for reimbursement of reasonable out-of-pocket disbursements incurred by the Firm in connection with the engagement. Disbursements may include, without limitation, filing fees (including Delaware Secretary of State filing fees for Certificates of Formation and other filings), messenger and courier charges, travel expenses (including transportation, lodging, and meals incurred in connection with travel reasonably necessary for the engagement), document production and reproduction costs, computerized legal research charges, and similar items. All disbursements will be itemized on the Firm\'s monthly invoices.

**4.4 Billing Procedures**

Invoices for professional fees and disbursements will be rendered monthly. All invoices are due and payable within thirty (30) days of receipt. Invoices will be directed to:

> Ardent Capital Management LLC 590 Madison Avenue, 28th Floor New York, New York 10022
>
> Attention: Finance Department

Copies of all invoices will also be provided to Marcus Aldridge and Priya Narayanan at the address set forth above, or at such other address or electronic mail address as the Client may designate in writing from time to time. The Client agrees to notify the Firm promptly if there is any question or dispute regarding any invoice, so that any such matter may be addressed in a timely manner.

**[5. Client Identity and Conflicts]{.underline}**

The Client for purposes of this engagement is Ardent Capital Management LLC. Calderwood & Harkness does not represent, and will not be deemed to represent, any individual principal of the Fund (including, without limitation, Marcus Aldridge, Priya Narayanan, or any other continuing principal), any departing principal (including David Kellner and Joanna Trask), any limited partner of the Fund, or any other entity in the Ardent Capital structure (including, without limitation, the Fund, the General Partner, HoldCo, GP Intermediate, or any portfolio company) in their individual or separate capacities. Each such person and entity should consult with its own independent legal counsel with respect to any matter in which its interests may differ from those of the ManCo.

The Firm has conducted a conflict check in accordance with its standard procedures and, as of the date hereof, has identified no conflicts of interest that would preclude this engagement. In the event that a conflict of interest arises during the course of the engagement, the Firm will promptly notify the Client and take appropriate action, which may include seeking an informed written waiver of the conflict from the affected parties or, if a waiver cannot be obtained or is not appropriate under the circumstances, withdrawing from the representation in whole or in part as required by applicable rules of professional conduct.

**[6. Confidentiality]{.underline}**

Calderwood & Harkness will maintain the confidentiality of all information provided by or on behalf of the Client in connection with this engagement, in accordance with the Firm\'s professional obligations and applicable rules of professional conduct. This obligation of confidentiality extends to all non-public information concerning the Fund, the General Partner, the ManCo, HoldCo, GP Intermediate, the principals (whether continuing or departing), the limited partners, the portfolio companies, and any other entities or persons about which information is provided to the Firm in connection with the engagement.

The Firm may disclose confidential information as required by applicable law, regulation, or court order, or with the prior written consent of the Client. In the event the Firm receives a subpoena, court order, or other compulsory process seeking the disclosure of confidential information relating to this engagement, the Firm will, to the extent permitted by law and practicable under the circumstances, provide prompt notice to the Client prior to making any such disclosure, so that the Client may seek protective measures or take other appropriate action.

**[7. Document Retention]{.underline}**

Calderwood & Harkness will retain engagement files, including correspondence, memoranda, agreements, and other documents generated or received in connection with this engagement, in accordance with the Firm\'s document retention policy, as in effect from time to time. Upon completion or termination of the engagement, the Firm will, at the Client\'s request and expense, return original documents to the Client or make arrangements for the transfer of files. Documents retained by the Firm may be destroyed in accordance with the Firm\'s document retention policy following the expiration of the applicable retention period, unless the Client requests in writing that such documents be returned or otherwise preserved.

**[8. Governing Law]{.underline}**

This Engagement Letter and the terms and conditions set forth herein shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to the conflict-of-laws principles thereof.

**[9. Termination]{.underline}**

Either party may terminate this engagement at any time upon written notice to the other party. In the event of termination by either party, the Client will remain responsible for payment of all professional fees earned and disbursements incurred through the date of termination, in accordance with the billing and payment terms set forth in Section 4 above.

Upon termination, Calderwood & Harkness will take reasonable steps to protect the Client\'s interests, including cooperating in the orderly transition of the matter to successor counsel designated by the Client. The Firm will promptly deliver to the Client or its successor counsel all documents and materials necessary for the continued handling of the matter, subject to the Firm\'s right to retain copies of such documents in accordance with its document retention policy and applicable rules of professional conduct.

**[10. Acceptance and Counterparts]{.underline}**

We respectfully request that the Client confirm its acceptance of the terms and conditions of this engagement by having each of the undersigned representatives execute and return the enclosed copy of this Engagement Letter to Calderwood & Harkness at the address set forth above, or by transmitting an executed copy by electronic mail to Nicholas Stern at nstern@calderwoodharkness.com or Graham Sutherland at gsutherland@calderwoodharkness.com.

This Engagement Letter may be executed in one or more counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original and all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument. Delivery of an executed counterpart by electronic mail in portable document format (.pdf) or by other electronic transmission shall be effective as delivery of a manually executed counterpart.

We look forward to working with you and the Ardent Capital team on this important matter. Please do not hesitate to contact either of us if you have any questions regarding the terms of this engagement or if you would like to discuss any aspect of the representation in greater detail.

Very truly yours,

**CALDERWOOD & HARKNESS LLP**

By: **\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_**

Nicholas Stern Partner

By: **\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_**

Graham Sutherland Partner

## Answer

**4 matters** qualify. I counted a matter when the matter materials show that the fund involved had an LP advisory committee (whether the client was the sponsor, fund, or an investor) **and** the applicable fund LPA was executed/signed. I did not count a draft-only LPA, an unformed/proposed fund, or a different type of committee (such as an Investor Advisory Committee).

| Matter | Fund | Why it qualifies | Key documents relied on |
|---|---|---|---|

The LPAC gave written consent on **February 14, 2024**, and **Amendment No. 1 to the LPA was executed on February 28, 2024**.
